children.translated_text: Having bowed to the goddess <s>Śāradā</s>, who is endowed with divine knowledge,
I shall tell, for the delight of the mind, an extract from the teaching approved by the parrot.
There is a city named <s>Candrapura</s>.
There a king named <s>Vikramasena</s> lived.

children.text: tasminnagare haridatto nāma śreṣṭhī tasya bhāryā śṛṅgārasundarīnāmnī
children.translated_text: In that city there was a merchant named <s>Haridatta</s>; his wife was named <s>Śṛṅgārasundarī</s>.
Their son was named <s>Madanavinoda</s>.
His wife was <s>Prabhāvatī</s>.
She was the daughter of the merchant <s>Somadatta</s>.

children.text: madanavinodastu atīvaviṣayāsaktaḥ kuputraḥ pituḥ śikṣāṃ na śṛṇoti
children.translated_text: But <s>Madanavinoda</s>, a bad son excessively attached to sensual pleasures, did not heed his father's instruction.
He was very much addicted to gambling, hunting, courtesans, liquor, and the like.

children.text: kumārgacāriṇaṃ taṃ kuputraṃ dṛṣṭvā tatpitā haridattaḥ sapatnīkaḥ atīva duḥkhitaḥ saṃjātaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that bad son walking on an evil path, his father <s>Haridatta</s>, together with his wife, became deeply distressed.

children.text: taṃ haridattaṃ kuputraduḥkhena pīḍitaṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya sakhā trivikramanāmā dvijaḥ svagṛhato nītinipuṇaṃ śukaṃ sārikāṃ ca gṛhītvā tadgṛhe gatvā prāha sakhe haridatta enaṃ śukaṃ sapatnīkaṃ putravattvaṃ paripālaya
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Haridatta</s> afflicted by grief over his bad son, his friend, a twice-born man named <s>Trivikrama</s>, took from his own house a parrot and a mynah skilled in policy, went to his house, and said, 'Friend <s>Haridatta</s>, care for this parrot, together with its mate, as you would for a son.'
By protecting it, your sorrow will go far away.

children.text: haridattastu taṃ śukaṃ gṛhītvā putrāya samarpayāmāsa
children.translated_text: <s>Haridatta</s> then took the parrot and handed it over to his son.
It was placed in a golden cage in <s>Madanavinoda</s>'s bedchamber and was well nourished by him.
Then one day, in private, the parrot said to <s>Madana</s>,
'Friend,
because your parents are grieving, streams of tears fall to the earth from their sorrow.

children.text: tena pāpena te vatsa patanaṃ devaśarmavat ||
children.translated_text: Through that sin, child, you will fall, like <s>Devaśarman</s>.'

children.text: sa prāha kathametat śuka āha asti pañcapuraṃ nāma nagaram
children.translated_text: He said, 'How is that?' The parrot said, 'There is a city named <s>Pañcapura</s>.'
There was a Brahmin named <s>Satyaśarman</s>.
His wife was named <s>Dharmaśīlā</s>, and their son was <s>Devaśarman</s>.

children.text: sa ca adhītavidyaḥ pitṛpracchannavṛttyā deśāntaraṃ gatvā bhāgīrathītīre tapaḥ kṛtavān
children.translated_text: He, having studied the sciences, went to another country while concealing his way of life from his father, and performed austerities on the bank of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>.
Once that ascetic sat down on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> for recitation.

children.text: tasminkāle kayācit balākayā uḍḍīyamānayā tadaṅgopari purīṣotsargaḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: At that time a certain crane, flying overhead, discharged excrement on his body.

children.text: sa ca tapasvī krodhākulitanetraḥ yāvadūrdhvaṃ paśyati tāvattatkrodhāgninā bhasmībhūtāṃ balākāṃ bhūmau patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā balākāṃ dagdhvā nārāyaṇadvijagṛhe bhikṣārthaṃ yayau
children.translated_text: When that ascetic, his eyes overcome with anger, looked upward, he saw the crane fallen on the ground, reduced to ashes by the fire of his anger; after burning the crane, he went to the house of the Brahmin <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> for alms.

children.text: svabhartṛśuśrūṣāparayā tatpatnyā kopābhiviṣṭo nirbhartsitaḥ satpakṣihāyam uktaśca nāhaṃ balākeva tvatkopasthānam
children.translated_text: There, angered by that man's wife, who was devoted to serving her own husband, he was rebuked and was told, 'Killer of a good bird, I am not a crane, a target for your anger.'

children.text: sa ca pracchannapātakajñānādbhīto vismitaśca preṣitaśca tayā dharmavyādhapārśva vārāṇasīṃ nagarīṃ yayau
children.translated_text: Frightened and astonished by her knowledge of his hidden sin, and then sent by her, he went to the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, to the side of the <s>dharmavyādha</s> (righteous hunter).

children.text: tatra raktāktahastaṃ yamapratibhaṃ māṃsavikrayaṃ vidadhānaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā dṛśāmantaḥsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: There, seeing him with hands stained red, like <s>Yama</s> himself, engaged in selling meat, he remained within sight.

children.text: vyādhena svāgatapraśnapūrvakaṃ svagṛhaṃ nītvā nijapitarau sabhaktikaṃ bhojayitvā paścāttasya bhojanaṃ dattam
children.translated_text: The hunter, after asking him welcome questions, led him to his own house, fed his own parents with devotion, and afterward gave him food.

children.text: tadanantaraṃ sa ca vyādhaṃ jñānakāraṇaṃ papraccha kathaṃ satī jñānavatī kathaṃ ca tvaṃ jñānavān
children.translated_text: After that, he asked the hunter the cause of his knowledge: 'How is that faithful wife possessed of knowledge, and how are you possessed of knowledge?'
The hunter said to him,
'Whoever properly practices the <s>dharma</s> (duty) handed down in his own lineage,
turning away from disturbances among the high, the low, and the middling,

children.text: sa gṛhī sa muniḥ sādhuḥ sa ca yogī sa dhārmikaḥ
children.translated_text: he is a householder, he is a sage, a good man; he is also a yogin and a righteous man.
And any ordinary creature who constantly serves his parents is such a one.

children.text: ahaṃ sāpi ca evaṃ jñāninau tvaṃ ca nijapitarau parityajya bhramanmādṛśāṃ na sambhāṣaṇārhaḥ
children.translated_text: I and she are both possessors of knowledge in this way; but you, having abandoned your own parents and wandering about, are not fit to converse with people like me.
Yet, regarding you as a supreme guest, I have spoken.'

children.text: evamuktaḥ sa brāhmaṇo vinayaparaṃ vyādhaṃ papraccha
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the Brahmin questioned the humble hunter further.
He said,

children.text: na pūjayanti ye pūjyānmānyānna mānayanti ye
children.translated_text: 'Those who do not honor those worthy of honor, and who do not respect those worthy of respect,

children.text: jīvanti nindyamānāste mṛtāḥ svargaṃ na yānti ca ||
children.translated_text: live while being blamed, and when dead they do not go to heaven.'
Instructed by that hunter, he went to his own home.
He became famous in the world, and afterward became a vessel of fame.

children.text: tasmādvaṇigdharmaṃ svakulodbhavaṃ smara pitrośca vinayaparo bhava
children.translated_text: Therefore remember the merchant's <s>dharma</s> born in your own family, and be humble toward your parents.

children.text: evamuktaḥ sa madanaḥ pitarau namaskṛtya tadanujñāto bhāryāṃ cāpṛcchya pravahaṇam adhirūḍhavān gato deśāntaram
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Madana</s> bowed to his parents, received their permission, asked leave of his wife as well, boarded a ship, and went to another country.

children.text: paścāttatpatnī katiciddināni śokayuktā nirvāhya svairiṇībhiḥ sakhībhiḥ pratibodhitā puruṣāntarābhilāṣukābhavat
children.translated_text: Afterward his wife passed some days filled with grief; then, awakened by her wanton female friends, she became desirous of another man.
For they spoke to her as follows:
'A man is father and kinsman only so long as he lives;

children.text: mṛto mṛta iti jñātvā kṣaṇātsneho nivartate ||
children.translated_text: when he is understood to be dead, saying, "He is dead, dead," affection turns away in an instant.'

children.text: atastvaṃ svapatim aprāpyamāṇā nijaśarīrasya katiciddinasthāyiyauvanasya puruṣāntararamaṇād gṛhāṇa phalam
children.translated_text: Therefore, since you cannot obtain your own husband, take the fruit of your body's youth, which lasts only a few days, through enjoyment with another man.

children.text: tatastāsāṃ vacanena puruṣāntarasya guṇacandrasaṃjñasya ramaṇāya śṛṅgāraṃ vidhāya yāvatpracalitā tāvatsārikayā mā gacchetyādivacanairnirbhartsitā
children.translated_text: Then, at their words, she adorned herself for the enjoyment of another man named <s>Guṇacandra</s>, and just as she set out, the mynah rebuked her with words beginning, 'Do not go.'

children.text: tato yāvatsā tāṃ sārikāṃ galamoṭanapūrvaṃ vināśayati tāvaduḍḍīya yayau
children.translated_text: Then, just as she was about to kill that mynah by first wringing its neck, it flew away and escaped.

children.text: tataḥ kṣaṇaṃ sthitvā sveṣṭadevatāṃ hṛdi smṛtvā tāmbūlaṃ pragṛhya yāvaccalitā tāvat śukaḥ prāha siddhirastu
children.translated_text: After that, standing for a moment, remembering her chosen deity in her heart, and taking betel, just as she set out, the parrot said, 'May there be success.'
She was asked with words beginning, 'Where are you to go?'

children.text: sā ca śukavacanaṃ śakunamiti kṛtvā prahasya tamāha he śukarāja narāntarāsvādaṃ vijñātuṃ pracalitāsmi
children.translated_text: And she, taking the parrot's words as an omen, laughed and said to him, 'O king of parrots, I have set out to learn the taste of another man.'

children.text: śuka uvāca yuktamidaṃ kartavyameva paraṃ duṣkaraṃ ninditaṃ ca kulastrīṇām
children.translated_text: The parrot said, 'This is fitting and indeed must be done; but for women of good family it is very difficult and blameworthy.'

children.text: kiñca tadā gamyatā yadi viparīte samāyāte sati tava buddhirasti
children.translated_text: Moreover, go then, if, when the opposite situation arises, you have intelligence.
If you do not have it, then you will fall into humiliation.
For:
Wicked people are always seeking curiosity when misfortune arrives,
just as in the case of the month-fasting woman when the merchant's son was seized by the hair.

children.text: papraccha sā tadā sārdhaṃ puṃścalībhiḥ kṛtādarā
children.translated_text: Then she, together with the wanton women, respectfully asked,
and in agitation said this: 'What is this that has been said, O parrot?'

children.text: yadi te kautukaṃ subhru parārthaṃ gaccha sundari
children.translated_text: 'If you have curiosity, O fair-browed beauty, go for another's sake;

children.text: sthirībhūya tvayā paścāt śrāvyeyaṃ mahatī kathā ||
children.translated_text: after you have become steady, this great story should be heard by you.'

children.text: evaṃ śukoktaṃ śrutvā yadā sā kautukākulacetasā nijagṛha āsīnāsti tadā śukaḥ kathāṃ prāha asti candrāvatī puraḥ
children.translated_text: When, after hearing what the parrot had said, she sat in her own house with her mind overcome by curiosity, the parrot told a story: 'There is a city called <s>Candrāvatī</s>.'
In it there was a king named <s>Bhīma</s>.

children.text: tatra sudhano nāma mohanaśreṣṭhisutaḥ tannagaravāsino haridattasya kalatraṃ lakṣmīṃ rantumīhate
children.translated_text: There, <s>Sudhana</s>, the son of the merchant <s>Mohana</s>, desired to enjoy <s>Lakṣmī</s>, the wife of <s>Haridatta</s>, who lived in that city.
That devoted woman did not consent.

children.text: tato māsopavāsinīṃ pūrṇābhidhānāṃ gatvā pūrṇadhanāvarjitāṃ kṛtvā haridatte nagarādbahirgate tadgṛhe dūtītvena preṣayāmāsa
children.translated_text: Then he went to a woman named <s>Pūrṇā</s>, who kept a month-long fast, won her over with abundant wealth, and, when <s>Haridatta</s> had gone out of the city, sent her as a go-between to his house.
She too won <s>Lakṣmī</s> over with flattering words.

children.text: prasannayā ca tayetyuktam yattvaṃ yācase tatkaromi
children.translated_text: And when she was pleased, she said, 'Whatever you ask, I will do.'
<s>Pūrṇā</s> said, 'Then enjoy the man who has become enamored.'

children.text: tayoktam kulastrīṇāṃ naitadyujyate paraṃ yattavāgre pratipannaṃ tatkaromi
children.translated_text: She said, 'This is not proper for women of good family; but whatever I have promised before you, that I will do.'
And it is said:

children.text: chijjau sīsaṃ aha hou bandhaṇaṃ caau savvahā lacchī
children.translated_text: Let the head be cut off, or let there be bondage; let <s>Lakṣmī</s> depart in every way,

children.text: paḍivaṇṇapālaṇe supurisāṇaṃ jaṃ hou taṃ hou
children.translated_text: in guarding what has been promised, for good men, let happen whatever may happen.

children.text: śīrṣa chidyatām atha bhavatu bandhanaṃ calatu savathā lakṣmīḥ
children.translated_text: Let the head be cut off; or let there be imprisonment; let fortune depart completely.

children.text: pratipannapālane supuruṣāṇāṃ yad bhavatu tad bhavatu ||
children.translated_text: In guarding an undertaking, for good men, let whatever may happen happen.
And likewise:
Let there be firm iron chains and various bonds of nooses,
yet stronger than those is the bond of speech for a good man.
Let there be firm iron chains and the binding of various nooses,
but stronger even than those two is the bond of one's word for a good man.

children.text: adyāpi nojhati haraḥ kila kālakūṭaṃ kūrmo bibharti dharaṇīṃ khalu cātmapṛṣṭhe
children.translated_text: Even now <s>Hara</s>, they say, does not give up the <s>Kālakūṭa</s> poison; the tortoise indeed bears the earth on its own back;
the ocean carries the unbearable submarine fire: the virtuous protect what they have accepted.
Hearing that, <s>Pūrṇā</s> was delighted.
'This is just so.'

children.text: tatastāṃ lakṣmīṃ pratividhāya guṇamohanārthe pradoṣe svagṛhe nināya
children.translated_text: Then, having instructed that <s>Lakṣmī</s>, for the purpose of delighting <s>Mohana</s> she took her to her own house in the evening.

children.text: tataḥ sa mohanaḥ kathitavelopari nāgataḥ kiṃcit kāryādivaiyagryeṇa
children.translated_text: Then that <s>Mohana</s> did not arrive at the stated time, because of some distraction with business and the like.

children.text: tato lakṣmyā sakāmayoktam yatkamapi naraṃ samānaya
children.translated_text: Then <s>Lakṣmī</s>, being desirous, said, 'Bring any man at all.'
Then foolish <s>Pūrṇā</s> brought her own husband himself.

children.text: svabhartari samāyāte sā kathaṃ bhavatviti kathaṃ gṛhaṃ yātviti tvaṃ sakhyastava vā kathayantu
children.translated_text: When her own husband arrived, how could she act, and how could she go home? You or your friends may tell.
They said, 'We do not know.'
'You yourself tell it.'

children.text: śuka āha yadi na yāsi tadā kathayāmi
children.translated_text: The parrot said, 'If you do not go, then I will tell.'
She said, 'I will not go.'

children.text: śukaḥ sā āgacchanneva svapatiriti jñātvā taṃ kacagrahaṃ pragṛhyaivamuvāca he śaṭha sarvadā tvamiti mamāgre jalpasi yanme tvāṃ vinā nānyā vallabhā asti
children.translated_text: The parrot said: 'As soon as she knew, while he was arriving, that he was her own husband, she seized him by the hair and said thus: O rogue, you always chatter before me that apart from me no other beloved woman is yours.'

children.text: adhunā tu mayā parīkṣito jñātaśceti kopaṃ cakre
children.translated_text: 'But now you have been tested by me and found out,' and she became angry.

children.text: sa ca tāṃ kaṣṭena sukomalavacanairanunīya svagṛhaṃ ninye
children.translated_text: And he, with difficulty appeasing her by very gentle words, took her to his own house.
Having heard the story told by the parrot, which caused fear and amazement,
the merchant's beloved slept at night, together with the group of wanton women.
In just the same way, together with them, on the second day at nightfall,
after asking the parrot, she set out, and the parrot said this to her:

children.text: yatheṣṭaṃ gaccha suśroṇi yadi jānāsi duḥkṛte
children.translated_text: 'Go as you wish, O fair-hipped one, if, in a misdeed, you know
how to make a reply when difficulty has arrived, like <s>Yaśodevī</s> in distress.'
Then <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks, 'Who is <s>Yaśodevī</s>?'

children.text: kadā kasminsaṅkaṭe tayā ka upāyaḥ kṛta iti
children.translated_text: At what time, in what danger, and what stratagem was made by her?

children.text: śukaḥ yadā kathayāmi tadā mayi suratavighātena tava kopaḥ prāṇaniṣūdanaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: The parrot said, 'When I tell it, your anger at me for interrupting your pleasure would be life-destroying.'

children.text: sā āha suhṛdāṃ sādhvasādhvapi śrotavyameva ityanujñātaḥ śukaḥ āha asti nandanaṃ nāma nagaram
children.translated_text: She said, 'From friends one must hear both what is good and what is not good.' Thus permitted, the parrot said, 'There is a city named <s>Nandana</s>.'
There was a king named <s>Nandana</s> there.
His son was <s>Rājaśekhara</s>.
His daughter-in-law was <s>Śaśiprabhā</s>.

children.text: tāṃ dhanasenasuto vīranāmā dṛṣṭvā sakāmaḥ san jvarapīḍito 'bhūt
children.translated_text: Seeing her, a man named <s>Vīra</s>, son of <s>Dhanasena</s>, became desirous and was afflicted with fever.
He did not undertake eating and the like.

children.text: sa ca mātrā yaśodevyā pṛṣṭaḥ sansagadgadaṃ kāraṇamāha sā ca rājakanyā durlabhā
children.translated_text: When he was questioned by his mother <s>Yaśodevī</s>, he, stammering, told the reason; and that princess was unattainable.
The question is: how could he live?
She said, 'You yourself tell it.'

children.text: śukaḥ yadi prabhāvati adya na yāsi tadā kathayāmi ityukte sā āha kathayeti
children.translated_text: The parrot said, 'O <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, if today you do not go, then I will tell.' When this was said, she said, 'Tell it.'

children.text: atha śukaḥ sā yaśodevī ekāṃ śunīṃ bhojanādyairāvarjayitvā ābharaṇāni paridhāyātmanā sārdhaṃ gṛhītvā śaśiprabhāpārśve gatvā tāṃ vijane sagadgadā jagādāhaṃ ca tvaṃ ca iyaṃ ca pūrvabhave bhaginyo 'bhūvan
children.translated_text: Then the parrot said: 'That <s>Yaśodevī</s>, having won over a bitch with food and other things, dressed it with ornaments, took it with herself, went to <s>Śaśiprabhā</s>, and in private said to her, stammering, “I and you and this one were sisters in a former birth.”'

children.text: mayā niḥśaṅkayā tvayā tu saśaṅkayā paranarābhilāṣaḥ pūritaḥ
children.translated_text: By me, without hesitation, and by you with hesitation, the desire for another man was fulfilled.
But by her, not at all.

children.text: ato 'syāḥ śīlaprabhāvātkevalaṃ jātismaraṇameva na bhogāḥ śunikā ca saṃjātā
children.translated_text: Therefore, through the power of her chastity, only recollection of her former birth arose for her, not pleasures, and she became a female dog.
And because of the interruption of enjoyment, recollection of your former birth does not exist for you.
But for me, because my enjoyment was unobstructed, my recollection of birth too is unobstructed.

children.text: ato 'hamanukampayā imāṃ śunakīṃ tvāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā kathayitumāgatā
children.translated_text: Therefore, out of compassion, seeing this female dog and you, I have come to tell you.
Therefore what is desired by petitioners must indeed be given by you.
Whoever gives a gift becomes the seat of all prosperity.
And it is said:

children.text: kathayanti na yācante bhikṣāhārā gṛhe gṛhe
children.translated_text: Those who live on alms go from house to house; they tell, they do not beg.
One should always give to petitioners; such is the fruit of one who does not give.

children.text: tataḥ śaśiprabhā sakaṇṭhagrāhaṃ ruditvā prāha māmapi kalyāṇi puruṣāntareṇa yojaya
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śaśiprabhā</s>, weeping with her arms around her neck, said, 'Blessed lady, unite me too with another man.'

children.text: tato yaśodevī tāṃ svasthīkṛtya bhartṛviditāṃ svagṛhaṃ nītvā svaputreṇa yojayāmāsa
children.translated_text: Then <s>Yaśodevī</s>, having reassured her and made the matter known to her husband, took her to her own house and joined her with her son.

children.text: sa ca rājaśekharo dravyādidānatoṣitaḥ sakhīyamiti kṛtvā na nivārayāmāsa
children.translated_text: And <s>Rājaśekhara</s>, pleased by the gifts of wealth and so on, considering her a friend, did not prevent it.
Thus, O fair lady, after deceiving the prince and the princess,
<s>Yaśodevī</s>, by great intelligence, accomplished her own purpose.

children.text: buddhirasti yadaiṣā te vraja subhru parāntikam
children.translated_text: If you have such intelligence, go, fair-browed one, to another's side.

children.text: bhaja nidrāṃ viśālākṣi mānyathā svaṃ viḍambaya ||
children.translated_text: Enjoy sleep, wide-eyed one; otherwise do not make a mockery of yourself.
Having heard this parrot's tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
Thus, in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>, the second tale.
Then on another day <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks the parrot.
The parrot:

children.text: gaccha deva kimāścaryaṃ yatra te ramate manaḥ
children.translated_text: Go, lady; what wonder is there, wherever your mind delights,
if you know how to protect yourself like the king?
<s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks, 'How is this?'
The parrot says: There is a city named <s>Viśālā</s>.
There a king named <s>Sudarśana</s> lived.
And there was a merchant named <s>Vimala</s>.

children.text: tasya ca patnīdvayaṃ subhagaṃ rūpasampannaṃ dṛṣṭvā kuṭilanāmā dhūrtastadbhāryādvayagrahaṇecchayā ambikāṃ devīmārādhya vimalarūpaṃ yayāce
children.translated_text: Seeing his two wives, fortunate and endowed with beauty, a rogue named <s>Kuṭila</s>, wishing to seize those two wives, worshipped the goddess <s>Ambikā</s> and asked for <s>Vimala</s>'s form.

children.text: labdhvā ca tatprakṛtiṃ vimale bahirgate tadgṛhaṃ gatvā prabhutvaṃ cakāra
children.translated_text: Having obtained his natural appearance, when <s>Vimala</s> had gone out, he went to that house and assumed mastery.
The whole body of servants was won over by favors and gifts of money.
Having satisfied the two wives with honor, gifts, and the like, he enjoyed them as he wished.

children.text: vimalo 'yaṃ dhanādyanityatāṃ śrutvā dātā babhūveti parijano 'navarataṃ cintayati
children.translated_text: The servants continually thought, 'This <s>Vimala</s>, having heard of the impermanence of wealth and the like, has become generous.'

children.text: atha satyavimalo 'pi dvāramāgataḥ kuṭilājñayā dvārapālena niṣiddhaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the true <s>Vimala</s> too came to the door, but by <s>Kuṭila</s>'s order he was blocked by the doorkeeper.
Then, standing outside, he cried out, 'I have been cheated by the king of rogues!'

children.text: tasya caivaṃ krandato gotrajā janāḥ kautukācca militāḥ
children.translated_text: As he was crying in this way, his kinsmen gathered out of curiosity.

children.text: tatkṣaṇāt haṭṭāni muktvā vaṇiksārtho militvā ārakṣikamantrimukhyānāṃ purataḥ phūccakre
children.translated_text: At once, leaving their market stalls, the caravan of merchants assembled and cried out before the chief ministers of police.
'O king, I have been cheated by the king of rogues!'
Then men were sent by the king to inspect the matter.
But he too made them favorable with gifts of wealth and the like.

children.text: taṃ dhanadāyakaṃ gṛhe dṛṣṭvā jano vadati svāminvimalo gṛhe vidyate
children.translated_text: Seeing the giver of wealth in the house, the people said, 'Master, <s>Vimala</s> is in the house.
And this king of rogues is standing at the door.'
Then the king had both of them brought together in one place.
Then no one among the two knew clearly which was the rogue and which was the other.
A commotion arose, destructive of all people's dealings, and a reproach to the king.

children.text: yato rājñāṃ duṣṭanigrahaḥ śiṣṭapālanaṃ ca svargāya
children.translated_text: For the restraint of the wicked and the protection of the good by kings leads to heaven.
And it is said:
The fire that has arisen from the burning pain of the oppression of subjects
does not turn back without burning the king's family, fortune, and life.
Then the king considered in private the determination between the two of them.
Now tell: how could certainty be attained? This is the question.

children.text: śukaḥ sa rājā labdhopāyastadvimalabhāryādvayaṃ pṛthakpṛthaksaṃsthāpya pṛṣṭavān kiṃ yuvayoḥ pāṇigrahaṇe bhartrā vibhūṣaṇaṃ pradattaṃ dhanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: The parrot said: That king, having found a means, placed those two wives of <s>Vimala</s> separately and asked them, 'At your wedding, what ornament and what wealth were given by your husband?

children.text: paścātkiṃ jalpitaṃ prathamasaṅgena ca kā vārttā bhartrā sahābhūt
children.translated_text: Afterward, what was spoken, and what conversation took place with your husband at the first union?
Who is your mother, and who is your father?
What is your family?
What is your caste?'

children.text: ityevaṃ pṛṣṭābhyāṃ yathālabdhaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ yathāproktaṃ yathāsuptaṃ sarvaṃ tābhyāṃ kathitam
children.translated_text: When asked in this way, the two women told everything as it had been obtained, as it had occurred, as it had been said, and as they had slept.

children.text: paścāttu tau puruṣau pṛṣṭau parasparaṃ visaṃvadantau
children.translated_text: But afterward the two men were questioned, and they contradicted each other.

children.text: tato bhāryādvayasya rukmiṇīsundarīnāmadheyasya yaḥ saṃvādaṃ vadati sa satyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the one who gave an account agreeing with the two wives, named <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and <s>Sundarī</s>, was the true one.
The other, however, was the rogue, and he was banished by the king.

children.text: satyastu rājñā sabhāryaḥ saskṛtaḥ svagṛhaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: But the true one, honored by the king together with his wives, went to his own house.
Thus was the wisdom of the great king.
Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
Then on another day <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks the parrot.

children.text: śukaḥ māṃ kṛtāvajñaṃ kṛtvā mā gaccha
children.translated_text: The parrot said: Do not go after treating me with contempt.
For even from a child a beneficial word should be accepted.
Long ago, O lady, a Brahmin who had treated advice with contempt and turned away from the words of elders
fell into calamity by marrying a poison-maiden.
<s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks, 'How is this?'
The parrot said: There is a settlement of Brahmins named <s>Somaprabha</s>.
There was a learned and righteous Brahmin named <s>Somaśarmā</s>.
His daughter, endowed with beauty, nobility, and virtues, became known as a poison-maiden.

children.text: tena tāṃ bhayena ko'pi na vivāhayati
children.translated_text: Because of that, out of fear, no one would marry her.

children.text: tataḥ somaśarmā varārthaṃ bhuvaṃ paryaṭan samprāpto dvijasthānaṃ janasthānaṃ nāma
children.translated_text: Then <s>Somaśarmā</s>, while wandering the earth for a bridegroom, reached a Brahmin settlement named <s>Janasthāna</s>.
There was a Brahmin named <s>Govinda</s>, dull-witted and poor.
The girl was given to him.

children.text: tena suhṛdāṃ nivārayatāmapi kṛtāvajñenoḍhā sarvarūpalāvaṇyaguṇopetā mohinī viṣakanyā
children.translated_text: Although his friends tried to stop him, he disregarded them and married <s>Mohinī</s>, a poison-maiden endowed with every beauty, charm, and virtue.
She was clever, but <s>Govinda</s> was foolish and young.
Then she lamented her own beauty, charm, and youth.
A foolish husband, a hero without virtues for mature women,
and scant wealth among virtuous and generous people: these bring sorrow.
Dwelling away from one's beloved in the month of <s>Pauṣa</s>, the days of youth, and poverty:
the separation from first love: these three are heavy sorrows.

children.text: appatthāve paḍhiaṃ kaṇṭhavihūṇaṃ ca gāiaṃ gīaṃ
children.translated_text: Study at the wrong time, a song sung without a throat,

children.text: mā mā bhaṇanti suraaṃ tiṇi vi garuāi dukkhāiṃ ||
children.translated_text: and lovemaking when they say, 'No, no': these three are heavy sorrows.

children.text: sānyadā govindaṃ patimityabravīt mama piturgehātsamāgatāyā bahūni dināni saṃjātāni
children.translated_text: One day she said this to her husband <s>Govinda</s>: 'Many days have passed since I came from my father's house.
Therefore I will go only together with you, and in no other way.'

children.text: tataḥ śakaṭaṃ mārgayitvā sabhāryakaḥ sa calitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after seeking out a cart, he set out with his wife.

children.text: yāvatprayāti tāvatpathi eko yuvā vāgmī surūpaḥ śūraśca viṣṇunāmā brāhmaṇo militaḥ
children.translated_text: As he was going, on the road he met a young Brahmin named <s>Viṣṇu</s>, eloquent, handsome, and brave.
Mutual passion arose between that Brahmin and her.

children.text: uktaṃ ca prītiḥ syāddarśanādyaiḥ prathamamatha manaḥsaṅgasaṅkalpabhāvo nidrāchedastanutvaṃ vapuṣi kaluṣatā cendriyāṇāṃ nivṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: And it is said: First there is affection from seeing and so on; then the mind's attachment and imagining; the cutting off of sleep, thinness, pallor in the body, and withdrawal of the senses;

children.text: hrīnāśonmādamūrcchāmaraṇamiti jagadyātyavasthā deśaitāḥ lagnairyatpuṣpabāṇaiḥ sa jayati madanaḥ saṃnirastānyadhanvī ||
children.translated_text: loss of shame, madness, fainting, and death: when the world reaches these ten states from the arrows tipped with flowers, victorious is <s>Madana</s>, whose other bow has been cast aside.
That traveler gave the couple a packet of betel leaves.

children.text: ityevaṃ grāmyabrāhmaṇorohaviṣṇor viśvastaḥ ātmano nirodhasaṅgabhayāduttīrya taṃ gantrīvāhamārohayati
children.translated_text: In this way, trusted by the rustic Brahmin, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, out of fear that his own obstruction and attachment would be discovered, got down and made him mount that wagon.

children.text: viṣṇunā ca patyau vṛkṣāntaragate sā mohinī bhuktā ātmavaśīkṛtā
children.translated_text: And when the husband had gone aside among the trees, <s>Mohinī</s> was enjoyed by <s>Viṣṇu</s> and brought under his control.

children.text: tayā cātmīyaṃ nāma gotraṃ kulakramaṃ cājñāpitaḥ
children.translated_text: By her he was made to know her own name, gotra, and family lineage.

children.text: patyuśca samāgatasya tvaṃ coro 'sīti gantryārohaṇaṃ kuvato niṣedhaḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: When her husband returned, she said, 'You are a thief,' and prevented him as he was trying to climb onto the wagon.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> too, taking her, overpowered <s>Govinda</s>.
Then there was hair-pulling between the two of them.
But <s>Govinda</s> was defeated by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, through the power of the poison-maiden.
Then <s>Viṣṇu</s>, taking her, set out toward his own house.

children.text: govindaḥ pṛṣṭhastho mārgāsanne grāme gatvā phūtkṛtavān yadanena caureṇa mama bhāryā gṛhītā
children.translated_text: <s>Govinda</s>, following behind, went to a village near the road and cried out, 'My wife has been taken by this thief!
Protect her!
I seek your refuge, good people!'
Then the village headman seized <s>Viṣṇu</s> together with <s>Mohinī</s>.

children.text: pṛṣṭenottaraṃ dattaṃ viṣṇunā yatheyaṃ mayā pariṇītā
children.translated_text: When questioned, <s>Viṣṇu</s> gave the reply, 'She was married by me.

children.text: madīyāṃ ca bhāryāmeṣa pathiko mārge dṛṣṭvā grahilo babhūva
children.translated_text: Seeing my wife on the road, this traveler became infatuated with her.'
When <s>Govinda</s> too was questioned, he answered this very same thing.

children.text: tato mantrī tayorekamevottaraṃ śrutvā jātyādikaṃ pṛṣṭavān
children.translated_text: Then the minister, having heard the same answer from both of them, asked about caste and the rest.

children.text: trayamapi tu saṃvadati tataḥ kathaṃ niścayaḥ
children.translated_text: But all three things agreed; therefore how could there be certainty?
This is the parrot's question.

children.text: tatastayā pṛṣṭaḥ śuka āha mantriṇoktam kiyanti dināni saṅgamasya yuṣmākaṃ prayāṇe
children.translated_text: Then, when asked by her, the parrot said: The minister said, 'How many days have passed since your union on the journey?'
They said, 'The union took place yesterday, after the meal.'

children.text: tato mantriṇā brāhmaṇau pṛthakpṛthakpṛṣṭau kimanayā kalye bhojanavelāyāṃ bhuktam
children.translated_text: Then the minister questioned the two Brahmins separately: 'What did she eat yesterday at mealtime?'

children.text: yacca tayā bhuktaṃ tadgovindo jānāti itarastu na
children.translated_text: And what she had eaten, <s>Govinda</s> knew, but the other did not.
Then he was exposed by the minister.
<s>Govinda</s> was instructed:

children.text: dhigimāṃ brāhmaṇīṃ paratreha ca duḥkhadāṃ muñca śīghram
children.translated_text: 'Shame on this Brahmin woman, who gives sorrow both here and hereafter. Abandon her quickly.'
And it is said:

children.text: vaidyaṃ pānarataṃ naṭaṃ kupaṭhitaṃ mūrkhaṃ parivrājakaṃ yodhaṃ kāpuruṣaṃ viṭaṃ vivayasaṃ svādhyāyahīnaṃ dvijam
children.translated_text: A physician devoted to drinking, an actor, one badly educated, a foolish mendicant, a warrior who is a coward, a libertine too old for such things, a twice-born man without recitation of the Veda,

children.text: rājyaṃ bālanarendramantrirahitaṃ mitraṃ chalānveṣi ca bhāryāṃ yauvanagarvitāṃ pararatāṃ muñcanti ye paṇḍitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: a kingdom with a child king and no minister, a friend who seeks deceit, and a wife proud of youth and attached to another man: the wise abandon these.
Even so, then despised by good men because he was greedy for a passionate woman,
he took that very woman and set out; for her sake he was killed on the road.
Therefore, O lady, one who in this way treats the instruction of elders with contempt
meets defeat, like the Brahmin <s>Govinda</s>.
Having heard the story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
Again on another day she asks the parrot about going.
The parrot said:

children.text: gaccha devi vijānāsi yadi kartuṃ tvamuttaram
children.translated_text: Go, O lady, if you know how to give an answer,
as the child-wise girl did in the difficult matter in the king's assembly.

children.text: prabhāvatīpṛṣṭaḥ śukaḥ kathāṃ prāha asti ujjayinī nāma nagarī
children.translated_text: Asked by <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, the parrot told a story: There is a city named <s>Ujjayinī</s>.
There <s>Vikramāditya</s> was king.

children.text: tasya rājñaḥ kāmalīlā nāma uttamakule jātā
children.translated_text: That king had a woman named <s>Kāmalīlā</s>, born in an excellent family.
And she was exceedingly beloved by the king.

children.text: ekadā nṛpastayā sārdhaṃ bhojanaṃ kurvanbhṛṣṭamatsyāṃstasyai dāpayāmāsa
children.translated_text: One day, as the king was eating together with her, he had fried fish served to her.

children.text: sā āha svāmin nāhametānpuruṣānavalokayitumapi samarthā kiṃ punaḥ sparśanam
children.translated_text: She said, 'Lord, I am not even able to look at these males; how much less can I touch them?'

children.text: iti śrutvā matsyā aṭṭahāsena tathā jahasuryathā nāgarikaloke śrutam
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the fish laughed with such loud laughter that it was heard among the city people.
And the king asks his ministers, astrologers, and those skilled in omens the reason for the laughter of those fish.

children.text: yadā na ko 'pi jānāti tadā sarvadvijāgresaraṃ purohitaṃ prāha yathā tvayaiva matsyahāsyakāraṇaṃ kathanīyamanyathā tvaṃ deśānnirvāsaṃ prāpnoṣi
children.translated_text: When no one knew, then he said to the royal priest, the foremost of all twice-born men, 'You yourself must tell the reason for the fish's laughter; otherwise you will be banished from the country.'

children.text: purodhā apyetadvacaḥ śrutvā dinapañcakaṃ vyavadhāne yācayitvā saviṣādo gṛhamagamat
children.translated_text: The priest too, having heard this command, asked for an interval of five days and, full of sorrow, went home.
That priest, not knowing the answer, was about to be banished by the king from before him.
How can he be saved? This is the question.

children.text: uttaramapyāha śukaḥ sa brāhmaṇo viṣādāpannaḥ putryā bālapaṇḍitayā babhāṣe tāta kathamudvignacitta iva lakṣyase
children.translated_text: The parrot also gave the answer: That Brahmin, overcome with grief, was addressed by his daughter, a child sage: 'Father, why do you appear as if your mind is distressed?'
'Tell me the cause of your sorrow.'
'The learned must stand firm even in calamity.'
And it is said:

children.text: sampadi yasya na harṣo vipadi viṣādo raṇe ca bhīrutvam
children.translated_text: He in whom there is no elation in prosperity, no despondency in adversity, and no cowardice in battle,

children.text: taṃ bhuvanatrayatilakaṃ jananī janayati sutaṃ viralam ||
children.translated_text: such a son, an ornament of the three worlds, a mother bears only rarely.

children.text: tato brāhmaṇo 'viralaṃ vṛttāntamācaṣṭe anena kāraṇena rājā māṃ nāgarānnirvāsayati
children.translated_text: Then the Brahmin related the whole matter without omission: 'For this reason the king is banishing me from the city.'
For:

children.text: na sauhṛdaṃ na viśvāso na sneho na ca bandhutā
children.translated_text: There is no friendship, no trust, no affection, and no kinship

children.text: kenāpi saha saṃsāre kuto rājñā chalārthinā ||
children.translated_text: with anyone in this world; how much less with a king seeking deception?
And it is said:

children.text: kāke śaucaṃ dyūtakāre ca satyaṃ sarpe kṣāntiḥ strīṣu kāmopaśāntiḥ
children.translated_text: Purity in a crow, truth in a gambler, patience in a snake, the pacification of desire in women,

children.text: klībe dhairyaṃ madyape tattvacintā rājā mitraṃ kena dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: courage in a eunuch, contemplation of reality in a drunkard, and a king as a friend: by whom have these been seen or heard?
Moreover:
In rivers, in clawed creatures, in horned creatures, and in those holding weapons,

children.text: viśvāso naiva kartavyaḥ strīṣu rājakuleṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: trust should never be placed, nor in women and royal households.
Enjoyers, attached to their sheaths, cruel, moving crookedly,
and approached with difficulty: kings are like snakes.
A king kills even while smiling, a wicked man even while honoring,
an elephant even while touching, and a serpent even while smelling.

children.text: eṣa rājā ā bālyātsevito 'pi mayi viparīto babhūva
children.translated_text: This king, though served by me from childhood, has turned hostile toward me.

children.text: tasmānmayā jīvitumicchatā dvijaiḥ saha paradeśaṃ gantavyam
children.translated_text: Therefore, since I wish to live, I must go to another country together with the twice-born men.
And it is said:
One should abandon one man for the sake of a family; for the sake of a village one should abandon a family.
For the sake of a district one should abandon a village; for one's own sake one should abandon the whole earth.

children.text: tataḥ sā bālikā tātavacanaṃ śrutvā prāha tāta tvayā yuktamuktam
children.translated_text: Then that girl, having heard her father's words, said, 'Father, what you have said is reasonable.'
'But those who are without a master are nowhere honored.'
For it is said:
An unimportant man becomes important if he serves a king;
even an important man becomes unimportant if he is without service.
A king favors the man who is near at hand, even if he is without learning, without family, or unknown;

children.text: prāyeṇa bhūmipatayaḥ pramadā latāśca yaḥ pārśvato bhavati taṃ pariveṣṭayanti ||
children.translated_text: for generally kings, women, and creepers embrace the one who is beside them.
Those who are near a king rise gradually, even if he shakes them off to death;
they discover the objects of his anger and favor.
And likewise:
For learned men, men of great ambition, men endowed with skill and valor,
and men who know the profession of service, there is no support apart from a king.
For those who, though high-born and energetic, do not approach a king,
begging until death has been prescribed as their expiation.

children.text: rogairgrahair nṛpairgrasto yo na vetti jaḍakriyaḥ
children.translated_text: He who, when afflicted by diseases, planets, or kings, does not know the dull man's action,

children.text: madhyamantramupāyaṃ ca so 'vaśyaṃ tāta na sthiraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the proper counsel, and the means, is certainly not secure, father.
And it is said:
Seeing snakes, tigers, elephants, and lions brought under control by stratagems,
what measure is a king to wise men who are not careless?
And likewise:
Only by taking refuge in a king does a learned man attain the highest advancement;
sandalwood does not grow well anywhere other than <s>Malaya</s>.
White parasols, charming horses,

children.text: sadā mattāśca mātaṅgāḥ prasanne sati bhūpatau ||
children.translated_text: and always-maddened elephants exist when the king is pleased.
Therefore, father, you are honored by the king and are an object of his favor.
So do not become despondent in this doubtful matter.
For:
When a royal summons has arrived and there is uncertainty in a difficult affair,
the chief ministers are the cutters of doubt for kings whose minds are uncertain.
Therefore, father, be firm.
The answer about the fish's laughter is to be spoken by me before the king.
Bathe and eat.

children.text: tataḥ sa evaṃ kṛtvā rājño 'grato gatvā sarvaṃ nivedayāmāsa
children.translated_text: Then, having done so, he went before the king and reported everything.
The king too, pleased, summoned her.

children.text: sā āśīrvādaṃ dattvā rājānamabravīt rājanmā mudhā viprānviḍambaya
children.translated_text: She gave a blessing and said to the king, 'O king, do not mock Brahmins in vain.'

children.text: kiṃ tvayā evaṃvidhaṃ matsyānāṃ hāsyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ vā
children.translated_text: 'Have you ever seen or heard of such laughter among fish?'
'How are you not ashamed, asking me, a weak woman?'
For even another king is not ordinary, bearing a divine form;
but you are <s>Vikramāditya</s>, rightly so called, scorcher of foes.
And it is said:
Taking sovereignty from <s>Indra</s>, splendor from fire, wrath from <s>Yama</s>, and wealth from <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,

children.text: sattvasthite rāmajanārdanābhyām ādāya rājñaḥ kriyate śarīram ||
children.translated_text: and firmness in courage from <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Janārdana</s>, the body of a king is made.
And likewise in the <s>Bhārata</s>:
Do not, O <s>Vṛkodara</s>, with your foot touch the lord of eleven armies,
who is the husband of all five; <s>Nāsā</s> is not an ordinary human woman.
Master, why do you not consider the matter yourself?
For you yourself are the remover of all doubts.
But if you have curiosity to hear it from others, then listen.
This queen, a woman of great chastity, does not touch these fish of ours,
O king; the śaphara fish surely laughed because of the account of a man.
O king, the meaning of this verse should always be pondered by you in your heart.

children.text: mūḍhadhīranyathā deva yadi pṛcchasi māṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O king, if, though dull-minded, you ask me again in this way,
how could there be a suspicion of unchastity regarding the king's wife, who had not even seen the sun?

children.text: ślokārthe prastutārthe ca matsyānāṃ hasanaṃ budhāḥ
children.translated_text: The wise understand the laughter of the fish both in the meaning of the verse and in the present matter,
but that king and the others do not understand it, though they know all matters.

children.text: tataḥ sado mūḍhaṃ dṛṣṭvā bālapaṇḍitā utthāya yayau
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the whole assembly bewildered, the learned girl rose and went away.
The parrot too said, 'I shall tell it in the morning.'
Hearing these words of the parrot, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
Then on the next day <s>Prabhāvatī</s> said to the parrot,

children.text: śuka sa matsyahāsyavyatikaro rājñā jñāto na veti
children.translated_text: 'Parrot, was that incident of the fishes' laughter understood by the king or not?'

children.text: śuka āha nṛpaḥ ślokārthamajānanna nidrāṃ lebhe
children.translated_text: The parrot said: The king, not understanding the meaning of the verse, did not obtain sleep.
And it is said:
Sleep, dear lady, whence can it come to those who are afflicted by debt and disease,
to those whose wives are disobedient, and to others who have made enemies?

children.text: rājā nidrābhāve kaṣṭena niśāṃ nītvā prātarbālapaṇḍitāmākārya prāha bālike ślokārtho na jñāto mayā
children.translated_text: The king, for want of sleep, passed the night with difficulty, and in the morning summoned the learned girl and said, 'Girl, the meaning of the verse has not been understood by me.
Therefore tell me the reason for the fish's laughter.'
She said, 'O king, do not ask me.
For:
There will be remorse here afterward, as there was for the merchant's wife
when she pressed her husband insistently about the coming of the cakes.'
The king asked, 'How is this?'
The parrot said: There is here a city named <s>Jayantī</s>.

children.text: tatra vaṇiksutaḥ sumatirnāma tasya priyā padminī nāma
children.translated_text: There the son of a merchant, named <s>Sumati</s>, lived; his beloved was named <s>Padminī</s>.
And that merchant's wealth was exhausted through the loss of his merit.
He was abandoned by people.
For people are friends of wealth.
And it is said:
He who has wealth has friends; he who has wealth has kinsmen.

children.text: yasyārthāḥ sa pumāṃlloke yasyārthāḥ sa ca paṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who has wealth is a man in the world, and he who has wealth is also a scholar.
And likewise in the <s>Bhārata</s>:

children.text: jīvanto 'pi mṛtāḥ pañca śrūyante kila bhārata
children.translated_text: Five, though alive, are said to be as dead, O <s>Bhārata</s>:
the poor man, the sick man, the fool, the exile, and the perpetual servant.
And likewise:

children.text: iha loke hi dhanināṃ paro 'pi svajanāyate
children.translated_text: In this world, indeed, for the wealthy even a stranger becomes one's own man;
for the poor, even one's own man at once becomes a bad man.
He too brought grass, wood, and the like and sold it in the middle of the city.

children.text: anyadā anena tṛṇakāṣṭhādikaṃ kimapi vane na prāptam
children.translated_text: One day he obtained no grass, wood, or anything else in the forest.
But he found an image of <s>Vighnavināyaka</s> made of hard wood.

children.text: tataścintitaṃ kimasau mama vidhāsyati uktaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Then he thought, 'What will this do for me?' And it is said:

children.text: bubhukṣitaḥ kiṃ na karoti pāpaṃ kṣīṇā narā niṣkaruṇā bhavanti
children.translated_text: What sin does a hungry man not commit? Men who are ruined become without pity.

children.text: prāṇārthamete hi samācaranti mataṃ satāṃ yanna mataṃ tadeṣām ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of life they do what the good consider improper and what these men do not consider improper.

children.text: yāvatsa tasya vināyakasya pāṭanāyottiṣṭhati tāvattuṣṭaḥ san jagāda ahaṃ tava pratidinaṃ pañca pañca maṇḍakāndāsye khaṇḍaghṛtayutān
children.translated_text: Just as he rose to split that <s>Vināyaka</s>, the god, being pleased, said, 'Every day I shall give you five cakes each, accompanied by sugar and ghee.
You should come to my shrine in the morning.

children.text: paraṃ kasyāpi idaṃ rahasyaṃ na kathanīyam
children.translated_text: But this secret must not be told to anyone.
If it is told, my promise will become false.'

children.text: so 'pi ca tatheti pratipādya nityaṃ maṇḍakapañcakaṃ bhāryāyā arpayati
children.translated_text: He too agreed, saying, 'So be it,' and every day he presented the five cakes to his wife.

children.text: taddaivaṃ maṇḍakapañcakaṃ ghṛtakhaṇḍayuktamādāya tadbhāryā nijakuṭumbaṃ tṛptīkaroti
children.translated_text: Taking those five divine cakes, accompanied by ghee and sugar, his wife satisfied her household.

children.text: nityaṃ ca tānmaṇḍakān gotriṇāṃ gṛhe vāhayāmāsa
children.translated_text: And every day she had those cakes carried to the house of her kinsmen.
She also sent them daily for the satisfaction of her own friend <s>Mandodarī</s>.
One day that friend asked her.
But <s>Padminī</s> did not know this coming of the cakes.

children.text: tatastasyāḥ purā sā sakhī kapaṭādbrūte sakhi yadi tvaṃ mama purato guhyaṃ na kathayasi tatkaḥ snehaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, in front of her, that friend deceitfully said, 'Friend, if you do not tell me a secret, what affection is there?'
And it is said:
Giving and receiving, telling a secret and asking about one,
eating and feeding too: this is the sixfold mark of affection.

children.text: tataḥ padminyāha madīyaḥ patiridaṃ guhyaṃ mamāgre kathamapi na brūte mayā śataśaḥ pṛṣṭo 'pi
children.translated_text: Then <s>Padminī</s> said, 'My husband never tells this secret before me in any way, though I have asked him hundreds of times.'

children.text: tayoktaṃ tarhi tvadīyaṃ jīvitaṃ rūpaṃ yauvanaṃ savamapi nirarthakameva yadidaṃ nājñāyi
children.translated_text: She said, 'Then your life, beauty, youth, and everything are entirely useless, since this is not known.'

children.text: tataḥ padminī patiṃ pṛcchati kathaṃ maṇḍakaprāptiḥ patirāha vidheḥ prasādāt
children.translated_text: Then <s>Padminī</s> asked her husband, 'How do you obtain the cakes?' Her husband said, 'By the favor of fate.'
And it is said:
Even from another island, even from the middle of the ocean, even from the end of the quarter,
fate, when favorable, quickly brings and joins the desired thing.
Moreover:

children.text: kṣutkṣāmasya karaṇḍapiṇḍitatanormlānendriyasya kṣudhā kṛtvākhurvivaraṃ svayaṃ nipatito naktaṃ mukhe bhoginaḥ
children.translated_text: A mouse, emaciated by hunger, its body squeezed into a basket and its senses withered by hunger, made a hole and at night itself fell into the mouth of a snake.

children.text: tṛptastatpiśitena satvaramasau tenaiva yātaḥ pathā svasthāstiṣṭhata daivameva hi nṛṇāṃ vṛddhau kṣaye kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Satisfied with its flesh, that snake quickly went out by that very path. Remain at ease: fate alone is the cause of men's increase and decline.
When he would not tell her, she undertook a fast.

children.text: patirāha asminkathite mahatī hāniḥ paścāttāpaśca bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Her husband said, 'If this is told, there will be great loss and remorse afterward.'

children.text: evaṃ bodhitāpi sā yāvannāgrahaṃ muñcati tadā tena daivopahatacittena kathitam
children.translated_text: Although instructed in this way, when she did not give up her insistence, he, with his mind stricken by fate, told it.
And it is said:
When the gods grant defeat to a man,

children.text: buddhiṃ tasyāpakarṣanti na sa vetyātmano hitam ||
children.translated_text: they draw away his understanding; he does not know his own good.
Thus, O king, after his judgment had been released by fate, he proclaimed the secret.
For one of diminished merit is abandoned by understanding.
And it is said:

children.text: rāmo hemamṛgaṃ na vetti nahuṣo yāne yunakti dvijān viprādeva savatsadhenuharaṇe jātā matiścārjune
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> did not recognize the golden deer; <s>Nahuṣa</s> yoked Brahmins to his vehicle; and in <s>Arjuna</s> there arose the thought of stealing from a Brahmin a cow with her calf

children.text: dyūte bhrātṛcatuṣṭayaṃ ca mahiṣīṃ dharmātmajo dattavān prāyaḥ satpuruṣo 'pyanarthasamaye buddhyā parityajyate ||
children.translated_text: In gambling the righteous one gave away his four brothers and his queen; generally even a good man, in a time of misfortune, is abandoned by his judgment.

children.text: sā ca patimukhāt śrutvā sakhīpurī jagāda
children.translated_text: Hearing this from her husband's mouth, she, <s>Sakhīpurī</s>, spoke.
And by her her own husband, holding an axe in his hand, was sent to <s>Vināyaka</s>'s side.
He too, together with <s>Padminī</s>'s husband, went there in the morning.
<s>Vināyaka</s> also bound both of them with peacock-bonds.

children.text: so 'pi ca padminīpatiruktaḥ re tvadīya evāyamanarthaḥ
children.translated_text: And that husband of <s>Padminī</s> was told, 'Sir, this misfortune is yours alone.'
'Therefore the punishment properly falls on you alone.'
Then <s>Sakhī</s>'s husband begged.
He gave those five <s>maṇḍakas</s> to him.

children.text: tau dvāvapi svaṃ svaṃ gṛhaṃ jagmatuḥ
children.translated_text: Both of them went each to his own house.
Then they were made to be given by the husband.
And afterwards he feels remorse.
Therefore you too, lord of kings, must not question me.
You will have remorse.
Consider this verse yourself.

children.text: iti kathayitvā bālapaṇḍitā utthāya svagṛhaṃ gatā
children.translated_text: After saying this, <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> rose and went to her own house.
Having heard the story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: anyasmindine prabhāvatī śukaṃ papraccha kīra punastanmatsyahāsyakāraṇaṃ rājñā jñātaṃ śrutaṃ na vā
children.translated_text: On another day <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot, 'Parrot, did the king again learn and hear the reason for that fish's laughter, or not?'

children.text: śukaḥ prāha prātaḥ punarbālapaṇḍitām ākārayitvā rājā prāha kiṃ tanmatsyahāsyakāraṇam brūhi śīghraṃ bālike sā cāha
children.translated_text: The parrot said: In the morning the king again summoned <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> and said, 'What is the reason for that fish's laughter? Tell me quickly, girl.' And she said:
'One should not act with divine compulsion; remorse will follow,'
'as once happened to a Brahmin whose mind was attached to <s>Sthagikā</s>.'
On the surface of the earth there is a city named <s>Vatsona</s>.

children.text: tatra vīrākhyo rājā tatra ca keśavo nāma brāhmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: There was a king there named <s>Vīra</s>, and there also was a Brahmin named <s>Keśava</s>.

children.text: tena kadāciditi cintitaṃ yadahaṃ pitṛdhanaṃ na bhokṣye
children.translated_text: At some time he thought, 'I shall not enjoy my father's wealth.'
And it is said:
The best are known by their own virtues, and the middling by their father's virtues;
the low are known by their maternal uncles, and the lowest of the low by their fathers-in-law.
Moreover:

children.text: piara viḍhattai davvḍai caḍḍiri ko ṇa karei
children.translated_text: Who does not make himself a enjoyer by spending the wealth arranged by his father?

children.text: saiṃ biḍhavai saiṃ bhojaai viralā jaṇaṇi jaṇei ||
children.translated_text: But rare is the mother who bears a man who earns for himself and enjoys for himself.

children.text: pitrarjitaṃ dravyaṃ bhoginaṃ kaṃ na karoti
children.translated_text: Whom does inherited wealth not make a enjoyer?

children.text: svayamarjayati svayaṃ bhuṅkte viralā jananī janayati ||
children.translated_text: Rare is the mother who gives birth to one who earns by himself and enjoys by himself.

children.text: ityavadhārya sa medinyāṃ babhrāma devatīrthaśmaśānanagareṣu dhanārtham
children.translated_text: Having resolved thus, he wandered over the earth, through shrines, pilgrimage places, cremation grounds, and cities, for the sake of wealth.

children.text: anyadā sa nirjane pradeśe prasiddhe śivacatvare karālāyāḥ śmaśāne ca paribhramya pariśrāntaḥ kapilakamaṭham apaśyat
children.translated_text: One day, after wandering in a lonely region, at a famous crossroads of <s>Śiva</s> and in <s>Karālā</s>'s cremation ground, he became weary and saw <s>Kapilaka</s>'s monastery.

children.text: tatra ca paryaṅkāsanasthaṃ tāpasaṃ dadarśa sa ca viprastasyāgre kṛtāñjalipuṭastasthau
children.translated_text: There he saw an ascetic seated on a couch-seat, and that Brahmin stood before him with his joined hands formed into a hollow.
The ascetic slowly released his meditation and spoke thus:

children.text: kiṃ kasmai dīyate loke trāyate ko bhavārṇavāt
children.translated_text: 'What is given to whom in this world? Who saves from the ocean of becoming?'
'Whose impossible thing is accomplished in this time, ah, for a guest?'

children.text: tataḥ sa brāhmaṇa ūrdhvabāhurjagāda tavāham atithirdhanārthī
children.translated_text: Then that Brahmin, with arms raised, said, 'I am your guest, seeking wealth.'

children.text: tāpaso 'pi taṃ vipram alpayācakaṃ dṛṣṭvā manasi duḥkhībabhūva
children.translated_text: The ascetic too, seeing that Brahmin as a small petitioner, became sorrowful in his mind.
And it is said:
Seeing noble petitioners made poor by requests for only a little wealth,
even givers of life are exceedingly distressed in mind.
Moreover:

children.text: ahihūo vi a vivaā karei suaṇo parassa upaāraṃ
children.translated_text: Even when overwhelmed by adversity, a good man does a service for another;
even when split into pieces, the sandalwood tree removes another's burning pain.

children.text: abhibhūto 'pi vipadā karoti sujanaḥ parasya upakāram
children.translated_text: Even when overcome by calamity, a good man does another a favor;
even with a thousand branches broken, a sandalwood tree removes another's heat.

children.text: tato yogīndro yadā tvametatsparśanaṃ kariṣyasi tadā hemnaḥ pañcaśatāni nityaṃ dāsyatītyuktvā viprāya paryaṅkīkṛtaṃ sindūramarpayāmāsa
children.translated_text: Then the lord of yogins said, 'When you touch this, it will give five hundred pieces of gold every day,' and handed to the Brahmin vermilion made into a couch-like lump.

children.text: uktaśca etattvayānyasmai na dātavyaṃ na kathanīyaṃ ca
children.translated_text: And he said, 'This must not be given by you to anyone else, nor must it be spoken of.'
'Otherwise it will turn back and come to me.'

children.text: tadarpitaṃ yadā sa dvijaḥ prātaḥ spṛśati tadā suvarṇaśatapañcakaṃ dadāti
children.translated_text: When that Brahmin touched what had been given in the morning, it gave five hundred gold pieces.
And he went to the city <s>Ratnāvatī</s>.

children.text: tatra sthagikāṃ nāma veśyāṃ nityaṃ kāmayate
children.translated_text: There he constantly desired a courtesan named <s>Sthagikā</s>.
But she did not know the source of his wealth.

children.text: kuṭṭinī pṛcchati hale eṣa vipraḥ kimapi vyavasāyādikaṃ na vidhatte
children.translated_text: The procuress asked, 'Girl, this Brahmin performs no trade or other occupation.'
'Then from where does he give us wealth, and why does he sport so lavishly?'
Then the courtesan questioned him.
The Brahmin did not tell her at all.
Then, by the courtesan's own arts and devotion, he was won over.
Then, when asked, he explained that the arrival of wealth came from the vermilion.
And she took the vermilion while he was asleep.
Then, when there was no wealth, he was thrown out of the house by the procuress.
And it is said:
What cleverness is there in deceiving those who have entered into trust?

children.text: aṅkamāruhya suptaṃ hi hantuṃ kiṃ nāma pauruṣam ||
children.translated_text: What manliness is there in killing someone asleep after climbing onto his lap?
That Brahmin, not seeing the vermilion, went crying out to the king's gate, saying, 'I have been robbed!'
Then a dispute arose.
The procuress said:
'That man is a rogue, greedy for my daughter; that man is without wealth.'
'Possessed by the seizure of the god of love, he says such an improper thing.'
'How can what is not credible to people of good qualities be credited by the king?'

children.text: paraṃ satyamidaṃ jātaṃ sindūraṃ dhanadaṃ yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'But this has turned out to be true, since the vermilion gives wealth.'
And when the people understood, 'This man is a foreigner,' he was banished.
And that vermilion went back to the lord of yogins himself.

children.text: tato rājanvikramāditya sthagikāprītinibandhanāttenākhyāte ca sindūre sthagikā naiva viprasya babhūva na ca sindūram
children.translated_text: Then, O King <s>Vikramāditya</s>, because of the attachment of affection for the little pouch, when he had explained the vermilion, the Brahmin had neither the little pouch nor the vermilion.

children.text: evaṃ tavāpi rājan ratiḥ prītiśca na bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: In just this way, O king, there will be neither enjoyment nor affection for you either.
Having spoken thus, <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> went home.
After hearing this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
Then on the following day <s>Prabhāvatī</s> questioned the parrot.

children.text: śuka uttaraṃ dadau devi bālapaṇḍitā dvitīye 'hni saṃyāte rājānaṃ prāha deva nāgrahaḥ kartuṃ yujyate
children.translated_text: The parrot answered, 'Lady, when the second day had passed, <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> said to the king, "Your Majesty, obstinacy should not be practiced."'
For:
A king should not be obstinate in an auspicious or an inauspicious act;

children.text: tadaṅgāni hi bhūtāni rājñāṃ hi mahatī tanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: for beings are his limbs, and the bodies of kings are very great.

children.text: ākhyāte ca tava mayā vaṇikputryā yathābhavat
children.translated_text: And I have told you how it happened with the merchant's daughter.

children.text: na bahirna gṛhaṃ rājaṃstathā te 'pi bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Neither outside nor at home, O king: so it will be for you too.

children.text: rājā pṛcchati kathametat bālapaṇḍitā prāha asti pṛthvītale tripuraṃ nāma sthānam
children.translated_text: The king asked, 'How was that?' <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> said, 'There is a place on earth named <s>Tripura</s>.'
In it there was a king named <s>Trivikrama</s>.
There was a merchant named <s>Sundara</s>.
His wife, named <s>Subhagā</s>, was exceedingly unchaste.

children.text: sā ca bhartrā gṛhānniryāntī prayatnena niyantritā
children.translated_text: And when she was going out from the house, her husband restrained her with effort.

children.text: tāṃ ca niyantraṇāt pūrvameko vaṇigyakṣagṛhe sthitaḥ sakāmāmabhajat
children.translated_text: Before that restraint, a certain merchant staying in a shrine of a yakṣa had enjoyed her while she was full of desire.

children.text: yadā ca bahirnirgacchantī patinā nivāritā tadā sakhīṃ prāha sakhi adya tvayā sa mānavo yakṣāyatana ākāraṇīyaḥ yathāhaṃ tatra gatvā taṃ rame
children.translated_text: And when, as she was going out, she was stopped by her husband, she said to her friend, 'Friend, today you must summon that man to the yakṣa temple, so that I may go there and sport with him.'

children.text: tvayā ca mayi gatāyāṃ paścādasmadgṛhaṃ jvālanīyaṃ yathā gṛhakāryāsakto jano māṃ gatāṃ na jānāti
children.translated_text: 'And when I have gone, you must afterwards set our house on fire, so that the people, intent on the business of the house, will not know that I have gone.'
'Meanwhile, after enjoying him as I please, I shall return.'
Then, because of the friend's message, that man came there.
She too arrived.

children.text: tadā ca gatāyāṃ tasyāṃ sā sakhī tadgṛhaṃ prajvālitavatī
children.translated_text: And when she had gone, that friend set her house on fire.

children.text: sa pumānprajvalane kutūhalī yakṣāyatanaṃ muktvā tatrāvalokanāya gataḥ
children.translated_text: The man, curious about the blaze, left the yakṣa temple and went there to look.

children.text: sā ca tatra sthitā samāptātmaprayojanā yāvatā gṛhamāgatā tāvatā gṛhaṃ dagdham
children.translated_text: She remained there with her purpose unaccomplished; by the time she came home, the house had been burned.

children.text: na gṛhaṃ na bahirbhūpa vaṇigvadhvā yathābhavat
children.translated_text: Neither home nor outside, O king, as happened to the merchant's wife,
so it will certainly happen to you, great king.

children.text: atha cet jñātena ślokārthena prayojanaṃ tadā kalye svayameva jñāpayiṣyāmi
children.translated_text: But if there is any use in knowing the meaning of the verse, then tomorrow I myself shall explain it.
Having said this, she went home.
After hearing this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: athāparedyuḥ savismayā prabhāvatī śukaṃ pṛcchati sma śuka kiṃ vijñātaṃ vikramārkeṇa matsyahasanakāraṇam śukaḥ prāha devi na kimapi rājñā svayaṃ jñātam
children.translated_text: Then on the following day, full of wonder, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot, 'Parrot, was the cause of the fish's laughter understood by <s>Vikramārka</s>?' The parrot said, 'Lady, nothing at all was understood by the king himself.'

children.text: tato rājā prātardvijasutām āhūya bālapaṇḍitāṃ prāha tvayā ityuktaṃ yattvaṃ svayameva jñāsyasi
children.translated_text: Then in the morning the king summoned the Brahmin's daughter, <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s>, and said, 'You said that you yourself would know.'
'But I have understood nothing at all.'

children.text: bālapaṇḍitā prāha yadi rājannevamapi mayā kathyamānaṃ na vetsi tataḥ śṛṇu
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> said, 'O king, if even in this way you do not understand what I am saying, then listen.'

children.text: puṣpahāso nāma mantrī sarvamantriṇāmagraṇīr nirdeṣo guptaḥ
children.translated_text: 'There is a minister named <s>Puṣpahāsa</s>, foremost of all ministers, faultless and imprisoned.'
'Why has he been restrained?'
The king said, 'This <s>Puṣpahāsa</s> has a name that fits its meaning.'

children.text: yataḥ yadā so madīyāyāṃ saṃsadi hasati tadāsyāsyātpuṣpaprakaro nipatati
children.translated_text: 'For when he laughs in my assembly, a heap of flowers falls from his mouth.'
'And this story became famous throughout the circles of other kingdoms.'
'Then they sent their own men to investigate the marvel.'

children.text: teṣu samāyāteṣu tena na hasitaṃ puṣpaprakaro 'pi nābhūt
children.translated_text: 'When they had arrived, he did not laugh, and no heap of flowers appeared.'
'For this reason there was imprisonment.'

children.text: bālapaṇḍitā prāha kenāpi kāraṇena mantriṇā na hasitam rājan tatkāraṇaṃ tvayā jñātaṃ na vā rājā prāha mayā kimapi na jñātam
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> said, 'For some reason the minister did not laugh, O king. Have you learned that reason or not?' The king said, 'I have learned nothing at all.'

children.text: bālapaṇḍitā prāha tarhi kathamidaṃ daṇḍaṃ kurvanpāpabhāk na bhavasi
children.translated_text: <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> said, 'Then how, while imposing this punishment, do you not become a sharer in sin?'
And it is said:
One should acquire a kingdom by <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), and should protect it by <s>dharma</s> alone;
from <s>dharma</s> a king attains the condition of being a refuge, removing every fear.

children.text: yathā āgrahānmāṃ matsyahāsyakāraṇaṃ pṛcchasi tathā tamapi pṛccha hāsyakāraṇam
children.translated_text: 'Just as you persistently ask me the cause of the fish's laughter, so ask him too the cause of his laughter.'

children.text: sa evātmīyahāsyasya matsyahāsyasya ca kāraṇaṃ vaktā
children.translated_text: 'He himself will tell the cause of his own laughter and of the fish's laughter.'

children.text: rājāpi tadvacanātpuṣpahāsaṃ mantriṇaṃ vastradānapūrvaṃ mantripade pratiṣṭhāpya matsyahāsyakāraṇaṃ papraccha
children.translated_text: The king too, because of her words, honored the minister <s>Puṣpahāsa</s> with a gift of garments, restored him to the minister's office, and asked him the cause of the fish's laughter.
The minister said, 'Although misconduct in the household should not be told,'
for:
Loss of wealth, mental anguish, and misdeeds in the house,
deception and humiliation too: a wise man should not reveal these.
'Nevertheless, the king's command is weighty.'
For:

children.text: prabhuḥ prītisnigdhāṃ dṛśamapi na pāpeṣu visṛjet kutaḥ ślāghyāmājñāṃ praṇayarasasāndreṇa manasā
children.translated_text: A lord should not cast even a glance softened by affection upon the wicked; how much less a praiseworthy command, with a mind dense with the flavor of love.

children.text: atītyādityāgniprabhṛti bhuvi dharmendriyamayaṃ nṛpākhyaṃ hi jyotiḥ prasabhamidamaindraṃ vijayate ||
children.translated_text: Surpassing the sun, fire, and the rest on earth, this royal light, composed of <s>dharma</s> and power, triumphs by force as something belonging to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: tato rājan me kalatraṃ narāntararataṃ jātaṃ tacca mayā jñātam tena ca duḥkhena na hasitam
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, O king, my wife became attached to another man, and that was known by me. Because of that sorrow I did not laugh.'
When the king heard this, he brought the queen with flower-hands and looked at her face to face.

children.text: sā ca tena prahāreṇa kapaṭamūrcchāṃ nāṭayati sma
children.translated_text: And with that blow she pretended a false faint.

children.text: puṣpahāso 'pi tāmavalokya sahāso babhūva puṣpotkaraśca samajani
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣpahāsa</s> too, seeing her, became laughing, and a mass of flowers arose.

children.text: rājāpi tāmāśvāsya kṛtakopo dvijātmajāsyaṃ vilokya mantriṇamavādīt kathamasmadduḥkhe sahāso 'si mantryapi sabhayamañjaliṃ baddhvābhāṣata rājan poṭakajanaistvadīyā rājñī rātrau nāḍikābhirāhatāpi na mūrchitā adhunā mūrchiteti hāsyakāraṇam
children.translated_text: The king too, after consoling her, feigning anger, looked at the Brahmin girl's face and said to the minister, 'How can you laugh in our sorrow?' The minister too, fearful, joined his palms and said, 'O king, your queen, although beaten at night with sticks by the men of the hamlet, did not faint; but now she has fainted. That is the reason for my laughter.'

children.text: rājāpi sakopo mantrin idaṃ tvayā dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ veti papraccha
children.translated_text: The king, angry, asked the minister, 'Minister, was this seen or heard by you?'
The minister said, 'Master, I saw this very thing.'

children.text: yadi svāmī na pratyeti tadā kañcukamuttāryāvalokayatu
children.translated_text: 'If my master does not believe it, then let him remove her bodice and look.'
When this was done, the king understood everything.
Looking at the faces of the minister and the Brahmin's daughter, he said, 'What is this?'

children.text: mantryāha svāmin yadidaṃ dvijaputryā gūḍhārthaṃ matsyahāsyakāraṇaṃ niveditaṃ tanmayā prakaṭīkṛtam
children.translated_text: The minister said, 'Master, that hidden meaning, the reason for the fish's laughter, which was told by the Brahmin's daughter, has been made clear by me.'
When this had been said, the king dismissed the assembly.

children.text: atha dvijasutāpuṣpahāsāvapi bhītahṛṣṭau svaṃ svaṃ gṛhaṃ jagmatuḥ
children.translated_text: Then the Brahmin's daughter and <s>Puṣpahāsa</s>, both frightened and delighted, went each to their own house.

children.text: tena ca rājñā tasyā mañjūṣāsthito naro dṛṣṭo vināśitaḥ
children.translated_text: And by that king the man who was hidden in her chest was seen and killed.
And she was expelled from her own residence.
The parrot said to <s>Prabhāvatī</s>:

children.text: tathā tvamapi kalyāṇi mā kuruṣva vṛthāgraham
children.translated_text: 'So you too, fortunate lady, do not make a futile obstinacy.
He who is intent on obstinacy in the world becomes embarrassed, like <s>Vikramārka</s>.'
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> went to sleep.
On another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, adorned for love, said to the parrot:

children.text: kiṃ kartavyaṃ mayā kīra tvaṃ vadādya priyaṃvada
children.translated_text: 'What should I do, O parrot? Tell me today, speaker of pleasant words.

children.text: yadi te 'sti sakhī yāhi śṛṅgārīva sahāyinī ||
children.translated_text: If you have a female friend, go, like a woman skilled in love, as a helper.'

children.text: prabhāvatyāha kathametat śuka āha asti rājapuraṃ nāma sthānam
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> said, 'How is this?' The parrot said, 'There is a place named <s>Rājapura</s>.

children.text: tatra devasākhyaḥ kauṭumbikaḥ tatkalatre śṛṅgāravatī subhagā ca
children.translated_text: There a householder named <s>Devasā</s> lived. His wife, <s>Śṛṅgāravatī</s>, was beautiful and fortunate.
The two were devoted to a bond made for mutual protection,
famous as women lusting after other men and in the business of love.

children.text: anyadā yāvatsubhagā upapatinā saha gṛhāntarvidyeta tāvadbahiḥ sthānāt patir jhiṇṭahasto gṛhadvāri samāyayau
children.translated_text: One day, while <s>Subhagā</s> was inside the house with her lover, her husband came from outside to the door of the house with a bundle of sticks in his hand.

children.text: tadā sā kathaṃ bhavatviti praśnaḥ uttaramāha śukaḥ tataḥ śṛṅgāradevyā sā nagnīkṛtya gṛhādbahirniṣkāsitā
children.translated_text: Then the question is: how was this to turn out? The parrot gave the answer: Then she was stripped naked by <s>Śṛṅgāradevī</s> and driven out of the house.

children.text: patirapi kimidamiti bruvāṇo 'tyādarāt śṛṅgāradevyā uktaḥ yattvayā etāni jhiṇṭāni devyā upavanādānītāni tata iyaṃ grahilā saṃjātā
children.translated_text: When the husband said, 'What is this?' <s>Śṛṅgāradevī</s> said with great respect, 'Because these sticks were brought by you from the goddess's grove, she has become possessed.'

children.text: tato yathāsthānaṃ gatvā muñca yathā praguṇā syāt
children.translated_text: 'Therefore go and leave them in their proper place, so that she may become normal.'

children.text: tataḥ sa mūḍho yāvadevaṃ kartuṃ bahirjagāma tāvattayā gṛhādupapatirniṣkāsitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, while that fool went outside to do just that, the lover was sent out of the house by her.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> went to sleep.
At the evening time on another day, the woman, maddened by desire,

children.text: vinayena śukaṃ prāha gacchāmi yadi manyase ||
children.translated_text: respectfully said to the parrot, 'I shall go, if you consent.'
The parrot said:
'You must certainly go; this is my decision.
When water is going down a slope toward its desired place, who can stop it?
Even after you have gone there, something extraordinary must be done by you,
just as <s>Rambhikā</s> formerly did something extraordinary for the sake of a Brahmin.'

children.text: prabhāvatyāha kathametat śuka āha asti dābhilākhyo grāmaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> said, 'How is this?' The parrot said, 'There is a village called <s>Dābhila</s>.
There <s>Vilocana</s> was the headman.
His wife, named <s>Rambhikā</s>, was fond of other men.
And because of fear of her husband, no one desired her.

children.text: tataḥ sā jalavyājāt ghaṭamādāya vāpīṃ yayau
children.translated_text: Then, under the pretext of fetching water, she took a pot and went to the stepwell.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca tatra surūpaṃ pathikaṃ bhaṭṭaputraṃ krīḍārthaṃ dṛṣṭisaṃjñayā babhāṇa
children.translated_text: Seeing there a handsome traveller, a Brahmin's son, she spoke to him by a signal of the eyes for the sake of dalliance.
He too, skilled in the movement of lustful women's glances, understood her intention.
And it is said:

children.text: udīrito 'rthaḥ paśunāpi gṛhyate hayāśca nāgāśca vahanti noditāḥ
children.translated_text: A meaning that has been expressed is grasped even by an animal; horses and elephants move when urged.

children.text: anuktamapyūhati paṇḍito janaḥ pareṅgitajñānaphalā hi buddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A wise person infers even what has not been spoken, for intellects bear fruit in knowing another's gesture.
Moreover:
With the navel area being made to tremble, with a glance charming to the heart,

children.text: puṇaruttapecchirīe bālaa kiṃ kiṃ ṇa bhaṇio si ||
children.translated_text: and with repeated looks, boy, what indeed have you not been told?
By her, who made the inner navel-region whirl with a glance delightful to the heart,

children.text: punarutprekṣamāṇayā bālaka kiṃ kiṃ na bhaṇito 'si ||
children.translated_text: and who looked again and again, boy, what indeed have you not been told?

children.text: acchīhiṃ cia bhaṇiaṃ hiaattthaṃ jo jaṇo ṇa lakkhei
children.translated_text: What is in the heart has long been spoken by the eyes; the person who does not notice it,

children.text: teṇa paḍibohieṇa e kiṃ kīrai ṇa kkhu alleṇa ||
children.translated_text: when he has been awakened, what can be done with him, since he is surely ignorant?

children.text: akṣibhyāṃ cirabhaṇitaṃ hṛdayasthaṃ yo jano na lakṣayati
children.translated_text: What is in the heart has long been spoken by the eyes; the person who does not notice it,

children.text: tena pratibodhitena ca kiṃ kriyate nu khalu ajñena ||
children.translated_text: when he has been awakened, what indeed can be done with that ignorant man?

children.text: tataḥ sa tadantikamāgatya jagāda bhadre kiṃ vidheyam sāha tvayā mama pṛṣṭhalagnena asmadgṛhaṃ samāgantavyaṃ mama patyuśca namaskāro vidheyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then he came near her and said, 'Lady, what should be done?' She said, 'You must come to our house following behind me, and you must make obeisance to my husband.
I shall do everything else.
You must say, "Just so."'
Having spoken thus, she entered the house.
He too entered the house and stood before her husband.
The husband was astonished.

children.text: tataḥ sā kumbhaṃ muktvā patyuḥ sakāśamāgatyābravīt nātha upalakṣasva enam
children.translated_text: Then she set down the pot, came near her husband, and said, 'Lord, recognize this man.'
He said, 'I do not know him.'

children.text: tataḥ sā prāha ayaṃ mātṛsvasuḥ suto yo mayā śiśutve muktaḥ
children.translated_text: Then she said, 'This is my maternal aunt's son, whom I left when I was a child.

children.text: sa dhavalo nāma mama milanārthaṃ samāgamat
children.translated_text: He, named <s>Dhavala</s>, has come to meet me.

children.text: tato mayā āliṅgya sarvāpi svajanavārtā pṛṣṭā
children.translated_text: Then I embraced him and asked all the news of our kinsfolk.
And he, being a Brahmin, speaks in this way.'

children.text: tataḥ patinā sānujñātā taṃ mahānasaṃ nītvā bhojanācchādanasaṃskāraistoṣayāmāsa
children.translated_text: Then, with her husband's permission, she led him to the kitchen and satisfied him with food, clothing, and courteous attentions.

children.text: patirapi tuṣṭaḥ prāha bhadra tvayā nijabāndhavasya mahatī bhaktiḥ kāryetyuktvā suptaḥ
children.translated_text: The husband too, satisfied, said, "Good woman, you must show great devotion to your own kinsman," and, after saying this, he went to sleep.
Then <s>Rambhikā</s> sat down on the Brahmin's bed.

children.text: tatastenoktam tvayā patyugre ityuktaṃ yanmadīyo bhrātā samāgataḥ
children.translated_text: Then he said to her, "What you said before your husband, that my brother has come,

children.text: tattvaṃ me pratipannā bhaginī pratipannaṃ ca nirvāhyate
children.translated_text: that you have acknowledged me as your sister: what has been acknowledged must also be carried out.
And it is said:

children.text: chijjau sīsuṃ aha hou bandhaṇaṃ caau savvahā lacchī
children.translated_text: Let the head be cut off; let there be bondage; let fortune depart altogether.

children.text: paḍivaṇṇapālaṇe supurisāṇa jaṃ hou taṃ hou ||
children.translated_text: In preserving what has been promised, for good men, whatever happens, let it happen.

children.text: chidyatāṃ śīrṣamatha bhavatu bandhanaṃ calatu sarvathā lakṣmīḥ
children.translated_text: Let the head be cut off; or let there be imprisonment; let fortune move away entirely.

children.text: pratipannapālane supuruṣāṇāṃ yad bhavatu tad bhavatu ||
children.translated_text: In preserving what has been accepted, for good men, whatever may happen, let it happen.

children.text: lajjijjai jeṇa maṇo mailijjai ṇiakulakkamo jeṇa
children.translated_text: That by which the mind is ashamed, that by which the order of one's own family is stained,

children.text: kaṇṭhaṭṭhie vi jīe mā sundari taṃ kuṇijjāsu ||
children.translated_text: even when life stands at the throat, O beautiful woman, do not do that.

children.text: lajjate yena mano malinayati nijakulakramo yena
children.translated_text: That by which the mind is ashamed, that by which one's own family tradition is defiled,

children.text: kaṇṭhasthite 'pi jīve mā sundari taṃ kariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: even when life is at the throat, O beautiful woman, you must not do that."
<s>Rambhikā</s> said, "Do not speak so.
For a woman devoted to father and mother is exceedingly rare;
