having become as father and mother, a desirous woman must be enjoyed by men."
And it is said:

children.text: kāmārtāṃ svayamāyātāṃ yo na bhuṅkte nitambinīm
children.translated_text: A man who does not enjoy a broad-hipped woman who is love-stricken and has come of herself
surely goes to hell, slain by her sigh.

children.text: so kiṃ va māṇai para mahila jo ṇavi jaṃpi emva
children.translated_text: What indeed does he think of another's woman, he who does not speak in this way,

children.text: sa kimeva manyate paramahilāṃ yo viparītaṃ jalpatyevam
children.translated_text: what indeed does he think of another man's wife, he who speaks perversely in this manner?

children.text: jo ṇavi māṇai.. so kiṃ va māṇai thī avarāi
children.translated_text: He who does not think ... what indeed does he think of another woman?
... do not make a break in our affection.

children.text: yo viparītaṃ manyate ... sa kimiva manyate striyamaparām
children.translated_text: He who thinks perversely ... what indeed does he think of another woman?
It is heard that <s>Rukmiṇī</s> formerly, love-stricken like <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
was taken even though she was a brother's wife; who can overstep desire?
Even <s>Virañci</s>, desiring his own daughter when tormented by passion,
is seen even today in the sky, assuming the form of a charming deer.
At the wedding, seeing <s>Pārvatī</s>, the beloved of <s>Hara</s>,
his seed too fell, and the <s>Bālakhilyas</s> were born from it.

children.text: tayaivaṃ bodhito mūrkhaḥ sa yāvadramate na tām
children.translated_text: Though instructed by her in this way, the fool did not yet enjoy her.
She cried out, "I have been robbed! Save me, save me, alas!"

children.text: tayā ca phūtkṛte kimidamiti kurvāṇo bāndhavaiḥ saha dhāvito bhartā
children.translated_text: And when she cried out, the husband, saying "What is this?", ran there with his kinsmen.

children.text: sa ca kathaṃ mucyate iti praśnaḥ
children.translated_text: The question is: how is he to be released?

children.text: uttaram evaṃ ca sa brāhmaṇaḥ sabhayaḥ sannataḥ pādayoḥ patito jagāda svāmini prāṇān rakṣa
children.translated_text: The answer is as follows: then that Brahmin, terrified, bent down, fell at their feet, and said, "Mistress, save my life.
I shall do what you wish."

children.text: evaṃ sthite sā dugdhasahitaṃ bhaktamaḍhaṇḍholayat antike jvalinamajvālayat
children.translated_text: When things stood thus, she stirred about rice with milk and kindled a fire nearby.

children.text: āgataṃ ca patiṃ jagāda asya viṣūcikā upapannā
children.translated_text: And she said to her husband when he came, "This man has been afflicted with cholera.
Therefore I cried out."
Having spoken thus, she showed the rice with milk.
The foolish husband too, seeing it, went away.

children.text: tataḥ sā patyau supte yadṛcchayā surataṃ cakāra
children.translated_text: Then, when her husband was asleep, she had intercourse as she wished.
And he too, under the pretext of illness, stayed for one month and afterwards departed.
Having heard this, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
Then on another day she set out.
The parrot said:

children.text: viparīte samāyāte yadi vetsi tvam uttaram
children.translated_text: If, when a contrary situation has arisen, you know an answer,

children.text: yathā śobhikayā proktaṃ vavvūle carite sati ||
children.translated_text: as was spoken by <s>Śobhikā</s> when the incident of the babul tree occurred, then go.
In this matter, in the village of <s>Nalauḍā</s>, there was a very wealthy potter.

children.text: tasya bhāryā śobhikā nāma paraṃ kulaṭā naralampaṭā ca
children.translated_text: His wife, named <s>Śobhikā</s>, was extremely unchaste and lustful for men.

children.text: sā patyau bahirgate upapatisahitā gṛhāntaḥ krīḍati
children.translated_text: When her husband had gone outside, she was sporting inside the house together with her lover.
And while she was in this situation, her husband came home.
The question is: what is she to do immediately after that?

children.text: śukaḥ prāha yadā ca tayā sa āgacchan jñānastadā upapatiruktaḥ ca tvaṃ vavvūlavṛkṣam
children.translated_text: The parrot said: when she knew that he was coming, she said to her lover, "You are the babul tree."

children.text: evaṃ ca sa tayo proktastathā cakāra
children.translated_text: And when she had said this to him, he did just so.

children.text: tasya ca vṛkṣe caṭataḥ paridhānavastraṃ vilagnaṃ nagno 'pi vṛkṣamārūḍhaḥ
children.translated_text: As he climbed the tree, his lower garment got caught, and even naked he climbed up the tree.
And when he had climbed the tree, the husband said, "Who is this?"

children.text: sā āha ayaṃ śatrubhirabhibhūto 'dhovastram api tyaktvā vavvūlamadhirūḍhaḥ
children.translated_text: She said, "This man, overpowered by enemies, abandoned even his lower garment and climbed the babul tree."

children.text: tataḥ samāgatya tasyāḥ patinā vṛkṣānmandaṃ mandamuttārya sa svagṛhaṃ preṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then her husband came and slowly, slowly brought him down from the tree and sent him to his own house.
And that rogue woman laughed, clapping her hands together.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
Then on another day <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot.
The parrot said:

children.text: vraja devi sukhaṃ bhuṅkṣva ardhabhukte patau yathā
children.translated_text: Go, lady, and enjoy pleasure, if you know an answer when your husband has half eaten,
as <s>Rājikā</s> made her plan, covered with dust.
There is a place named <s>Nāgapura</s>.
There was a certain merchant there.
His wife, named <s>Rājikā</s>, was beautiful but extremely ill-conducted.
And the merchant's son did not know that she was attached to another man.

children.text: tataśca ekadā sa bhojanāya yadopaviṣṭastadā upapatiḥ kṛtasaṃketo mārge gacchan tayā dṛṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Then one day, when he had sat down to eat, she saw her lover, with whom she had made an appointment, going along the road.

children.text: taṃ ta dṛṣṭvā gṛhe 'dya dhṛtaṃ nāsti ityuktvā dravyaṃ tatsakāśādādāya ghṛtānayanadambhena veśmato nirgatya ca sā bahirjāreṇa saha ciraṃ sthitā
children.translated_text: Seeing him, she said, "There is no ghee in the house today," took money from him, and, under the pretext of bringing ghee, went out from the house and stayed outside for a long time with her lover.
But her husband at home was hungry and angry.

children.text: tataḥ sā kathaṃ gṛhaṃ gantumarhati iti praśnaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore the question is: how can she properly go back home?

children.text: uttaram tataḥ sā hastau pādau mukhaṃ ca dhūlidhūsaraṃ vidhāya sadrammā dhūliṃ gṛhītvā gṛhamāgatā
children.translated_text: The answer: then she made her hands, feet, and face gray with dust, took some dust along with money, and came home.
Her husband, angry and red-eyed, said, 'What is this?'

children.text: sā ca saniḥśvāsaṃ rudatī dhūlipuñjaṃ darśayitvā idamuvāca yatkṛte tvaṃ kruddhaḥ sa te dravyo 'tra dhūlyāṃ patitaḥ
children.translated_text: And she, sighing and weeping, pointed to the heap of dust and said this: 'The thing over which you are angry has fallen here in the dust.'
'Lift this up and take it yourself.'

children.text: evamuktaḥ sa vilakṣaḥ tadaṅgāni vastrāñcalena saṃmārjya sāntvayāmāsa vividhalālanaiḥ
children.translated_text: When she had spoken thus, he was embarrassed; he wiped her limbs with the hem of his garment and comforted her with various endearments.
After hearing this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
On the next day that broad-hipped woman set out.

children.text: śukenoktam yuktameva viśālākṣi paraṃ rantuṃ yadṛcchayā
children.translated_text: The parrot said, 'It is quite proper, wide-eyed one, that you should go to enjoy pleasure at will,'
'if, when your husband comes, you know how to speak as <s>Dhanaśrī</s> did.'
<s>Prabhāvatī</s> said, 'What is this?'
The parrot said, 'There is a city named <s>Padmāvatī</s>.'
There lived a merchant named <s>Dhanavāla</s>.
His wife, dearer to him even than his life, was named <s>Dhanaśrī</s>.
That couple, filled with mutual affection, used to sport together.

children.text: anyadā tu vaṇigdravyasāramādāya tāmāpṛcchya deśāntaraṃ jagāma
children.translated_text: But once the merchant took the best of his goods, took leave of her, and went to another country.
When he had gone, she remained in the house as though lifeless.

children.text: na snāti na ca sā bhuṅkte na jalpati sakhīsamam
children.translated_text: She did not bathe, nor did she eat, nor did she talk with her friends.
She had cast off every adornment and turned away even from her own body.
Mounted on the Malaya breeze, with the calls of cuckoos as its kettledrum,
with the fragrance of jasmine as its messenger and the humming of bees as its auspicious music,

children.text: anyadā tu samāyāto vasantaḥ kālarāṭ kṣitau
children.translated_text: once spring arrived upon the earth, the night of doom for the season,
in which even the minds of self-controlled men, they say, undergo alteration.

children.text: tasminvasantotsave gṛhopari sthitā nagarīrāmaṇīyakamālokya yauvanaṃ rūpaṃ ca nininda
children.translated_text: At that spring festival, standing on the roof of the house and looking at the loveliness of the city, she reproached her youth and beauty.

children.text: sakhī ca tadiṅgitajñā jagāda bhāmini rūpaṃ vayaśca mā vyarthaṃ vidhehi
children.translated_text: And her friend, knowing her signs, said, 'Lovely woman, do not make your beauty and youth useless.'
'For listen, round-thighed one: the kettledrum of the cuckoo's cry is being beaten,'
'as if by spring on earth for King <s>Madana</s>.'

children.text: muñcantu māninaḥ sarve mānaṃ sevantu vallabhāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Let all proud women abandon pride; let them attend upon their beloveds.'

children.text: gatvaraṃ yauvanaṃ loke jīvitaṃ ca tathā calam ||
children.translated_text: 'Youth in the world is fleeting, and life is just as unstable.'

children.text: tatastvamapi kuru vayaḥsāphalyamityukte dhanaśrīrjagāda nāhaṃ vilambituṃ sahāmi
children.translated_text: Then, when she had been told, 'Therefore you too should make your youth fruitful,' <s>Dhanaśrī</s> said, 'I cannot endure delay.'
'Do quickly whatever can be done by you.'
Then by that friend she was joined with another man.

children.text: yadā ca sā tenātmāsaktā jñātā tadā tadīyaśiroveṇī chinnā
children.translated_text: And when it was known that she was attached to him, her braid of hair was cut off.
Just then her husband came back from the other country.
The question is: what was she to do then?

children.text: śukaḥ prāha yadā ca patirgṛhadvāramāyayau tadā tayottaraṃ vicintyoktam nātha tvayā tāvadgṛhadvāri sthīyatāṃ yāvatsarvaṃ sajjaṃ vidhīyate
children.translated_text: The parrot said, 'When her husband came to the door of the house, she thought out an answer and said, "Lord, please stand at the door of the house until everything is made ready."'

children.text: tena caivaṃ pratipanne sā madhye gatvā bhaṭṭārikāṃ pūjayitvā purato veṇīṃ sthāpayāmāsa
children.translated_text: When he agreed to this, she went inside, worshipped the goddess, and placed the braid in front of her.

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā bahirnirgatya caraṇamaṇḍakaiḥ patiṃ gṛhāntardevīpurato nītvā jagāda nātha pūjaya gṛhādhidevatām
children.translated_text: Having done this, she came outside, led her husband by auspicious foot-circles into the house before the goddess, and said, 'Lord, worship the household deity.'

children.text: tena pūjayatā veṇīṃ dṛṣṭvā uktaṃ kimidamiti
children.translated_text: As he was worshipping, he saw the braid and said, 'What is this?'
She said, 'I had made a vow:'

children.text: yadā me patiḥ sameṣyati tadā svāminyahaṃ tavāgre veṇīṃ chetsyāmi
children.translated_text: '"When my husband returns, then, mistress, I shall cut off my braid before you."'
'Now I have done that.'

children.text: sa ca mugdho devīṃ namaskṛtya tāṃ bahu mānayāmāsa
children.translated_text: And that simpleton bowed to the goddess and honored her greatly.
After hearing this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
On another day she set out.

children.text: hasannāha śuko yāhi yadi kartuṃ tvamuttaram
children.translated_text: Laughing, the parrot said, 'Go, if you know how to make a reply,'
'as <s>Śriyādevī</s> did when her anklet had been taken.'
There is a city named <s>Śālipura</s>.
There lived a merchant <s>Śāliga</s>.
His wife was <s>Jayikā</s>.
They had a son named <s>Guṇākara</s>.
His wife was <s>Śriyādevī</s>.

children.text: sā cāpareṇa subuddhināmnā vaṇijā saha ramate
children.translated_text: She used to sport with another merchant named <s>Subuddhi</s>.

children.text: tato lokāpavāde 'pi saṃjāte 'nuraktastadīyaḥ patirna kimapi karṇe karoti
children.translated_text: Then, even when public scandal arose, her husband, being attached to her, paid no attention to anything.
And it is said:

children.text: rattā picchanti guṇā dosā picchanti je virattatti
children.translated_text: Those who are attached ask about virtues; those who are estranged ask about faults.

children.text: majjhatthā uṇa purisā dosā vi guṇā vi picchanti ||
children.translated_text: But impartial men see both faults and virtues.

children.text: raktāḥ pṛcchanti guṇān doṣān pṛcchanti ye viraktāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who are attached ask about virtues; those who are estranged ask about faults.

children.text: madhyasthāḥ punaḥ puruṣā doṣānapi guṇānapi pṛcchanti ||
children.translated_text: But impartial men ask about both faults and virtues.
Moreover:

children.text: mahilārattā purisā cheā vi ṇa saṃbharanti appāṇaṃ
children.translated_text: Men attached to women, even if clever, do not remember themselves.

children.text: iare uṇa taruṇīṇaṃ purisā salilaṃ va hatthagaaṃ ||
children.translated_text: But other men are like water held in the hands of young women.

children.text: mahilāraktāḥ puruṣāśchekā api na saṃbharanti ātmanām
children.translated_text: Men attached to women, even if clever, do not keep themselves in mind.
Other men, however, are for young women just like water held in the hand.

children.text: anyadā sā śvaśureṇa narāntarasahitā suptā dṛṣṭā
children.translated_text: Once she was seen by her father-in-law sleeping together with another man.

children.text: tataścaraṇānnūpuraṃ śvaśureṇa cottāritaṃ tayā ca jñātam
children.translated_text: Then the anklet was removed from her foot by her father-in-law, and she noticed it.

children.text: tataḥ sā taṃ jāraṃ prasthāpya bhartāraṃ tatrānīya tena saha suptā
children.translated_text: After that she sent that lover away, brought her husband there, and slept with him.

children.text: nidrāntare ca patirutthāpitaḥ kathitaṃ ca tvadīyena pitrā nūpuramasmatpādād avatārya gṛhītam
children.translated_text: During his sleep her husband was awakened, and she said, 'Your father has taken down the anklet from my foot and carried it off.'

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ ca pātakaṃ kvāpi na dṛṣṭaṃ yadvadhūpādāt śvaśuro nūpuraṃ gṛhṇāti
children.translated_text: 'Nowhere has such a sin been seen, that a father-in-law takes an anklet from his daughter-in-law's foot.'
He said, 'In the morning I shall make my father hand it over himself.'

children.text: tena ca guṇākareṇa pitaraṃ nirbhartsya tatsakāśānnūpuraṃ yācitam
children.translated_text: And that <s>Guṇākara</s>, after rebuking his father, demanded the anklet from him.

children.text: pitrā coktaṃ yadiyaṃ parapuruṣeṇa saha suptā dṛṣṭā ato mayā nūpuraṃ gṛhītam
children.translated_text: His father said, 'This woman was seen sleeping with another man; therefore I took the anklet.'
She said, 'I was sleeping with your son.'
'For this matter I shall undergo an ordeal.'
'Right here in the village, in the northern direction, there is a <s>yakṣa</s>.'
I shall come out from between his thighs.

children.text: yaḥ kaścitsatyo bhavati sa jaṅghayorantarān niṣkrāmyatīti prasiddham
children.translated_text: It is well known that whoever is truthful comes out from between the thighs.

children.text: evaṃ śvaśureṇa cāṅgīkṛte sā kulaṭā sati dine jārasya gṛhe gatvā tamuvāca bho kānta prātarahaṃ divyārthaṃ yakṣasya jaṅghāntarānnirgamiṣyāmi
children.translated_text: When this had thus been accepted by her father-in-law, that unchaste woman, on the proper day, went to her lover's house and said to him, "Dear beloved, tomorrow, for the sake of the ordeal, I shall come out from between the thighs of the <s>yakṣa</s>.

children.text: tvayā tatra samāgatya vātūlatvamāśritya mama kaṇṭhagraho vidheyaḥ
children.translated_text: You must come there, assume the state of a madman, and seize my throat."
When he had agreed to this, she returned to her own house.

children.text: atha prāpaḥ samastamahājanaṃ malayitvā puṣpākṣatādikam ādāya yakṣāyatane gatvā samīpasarasi snānaṃ kṛtvā yakṣapūjārthaṃ samāgacchantyāstasyāḥ pūrvasaṃketito jāro grahilībhūtastatkaṇṭhe nijabāhudvayaṃ yojayāmāsa
children.translated_text: Then, after gathering all the townspeople and taking flowers, unbroken rice, and the like, she went to the shrine of the <s>yakṣa</s>; and as she was coming back for the worship of the <s>yakṣa</s> after bathing in the nearby pond, her lover, with whom she had previously arranged the sign, became like one possessed and put both his arms around her neck.

children.text: tata āḥ kimetadityabhidhāya sā punaḥ snānārthaṃ yayau
children.translated_text: Then, saying "Ah! What is this?", she went again to bathe.

children.text: so 'pi grahilo lokaiḥ kaṇṭhe gṛhītvā tasmātpradeśāddūrīkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: He too, as a madman, was seized by the throat by the people and removed far from that place.

children.text: sāpi snānaṃ kṛtvā yakṣasamīpamāgatya puṣpagandhādyairabhyarcya sarvalokānāṃ śṛṇvatāmuvāca bho bhagavanyakṣa nijabhartāramenaṃ ca grahilaṃ vinā yadyanyapuruṣaḥ spṛśati kadācana māṃ tadā tava jaṅghābhyāṃ sakāśānmama niṣkramaṇaṃ mā bhavatvityabhidhāya sarvalokasamakṣameva jaṅghayormadhye praviśya niṣkrāntā
children.translated_text: She too, after bathing, came near the <s>yakṣa</s>, worshipped him with flowers, perfumes, and the like, and, while all the people listened, said, "Revered lord <s>yakṣa</s>, if any man other than my own husband and this madman ever touches me, then may my coming out from near your two thighs not take place." Having said this, in the sight of all the people, she entered between his thighs and came out.

children.text: yakṣo 'pi tadbuddhi manasi ślāghamāna eva sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>yakṣa</s> too remained there, praising her cleverness in his mind.

children.text: sāpi satīti samastalokaiḥ pūjitā svabhavanaṃ jagāma
children.translated_text: And she, as a faithful wife, was honored by all the people and went to her own house.

children.text: evaṃ cet śriyādevīvatkartuṃ jānāsi tadā vraja
children.translated_text: So, if you know how to act like <s>Śriyādevī</s>, then go.
Having heard this, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: anyadā sā calitā śukaṃ prāha śukāhaṃ narāntaraṃ gamiṣyāmi
children.translated_text: On another day, when she had set out, she said to the parrot, "Parrot, I am going to another man."

children.text: śukaḥ prāha satyameva tvayābhāṇi kartavyaṃ yanmano'nugam
children.translated_text: The parrot said, "What you have said is perfectly true; what follows the mind must be done.
For the mind, foolish woman, torments impossible things enough, as <s>Mugdhikā</s>'s did."
Hearing that, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> said, "How was that?"
He said, "There is a city named <s>Vidiśā</s>.
In it there was a merchant named <s>Janavallabha</s>.

children.text: tasya bhāryā mugdhikā nāma capalā svairiṇī
children.translated_text: His wife, named <s>Mugdhikā</s>, was fickle and unrestrained.

children.text: yadā ca tayātiśayena vidūṣito 'yaṃ tadā bandhūnāṃ kathayāmāsa yadiyaṃ bahiḥśāyinī
children.translated_text: And when he had been greatly disgraced by her, he told his kinsmen, "This woman sleeps outside."

children.text: yadā ca tairevamuktā tadā tayāpyuktam ayameva bahiḥśāyī sadaiva
children.translated_text: And when they said this to her, she too said, "It is he himself who always sleeps outside.
He slanders me falsely."

children.text: tatastairmilitvā nirbandhaḥ kṛtaḥ yaḥ ko 'pi adyaprabhṛti bahiḥśāyī so 'parādhī
children.translated_text: Then they assembled and made a rule: "Whoever sleeps outside from today onward is the guilty one."

children.text: evaṃ nirbandhe kṛte 'pi sā suptaṃ patiṃ vihāya bahirgatā
children.translated_text: Even after the rule had been made in this way, she left her sleeping husband and went outside.

children.text: tasyāṃ ca bahirgatāyāṃ sa patirdvāraṃ gatvā suptaḥ
children.translated_text: When she had gone outside, her husband went to the door and lay down there.

children.text: yadā ca bahiḥ krīḍāṃ kṛtvā samāgatāyāḥ sa patirdvāraṃ nodghāṭayati tadā sā kūpe dṛṣadaṃ kṣiptvā dvāradeśa eva sthitā
children.translated_text: And when, after amusing herself outside, she returned and her husband did not open the door, she threw a stone into the well and remained standing right by the door.

children.text: patirapi kūpe patitā bhaviṣyatīti jñātvā dvāramudghāṭyabahirnirgataḥ
children.translated_text: Her husband, thinking that she must have fallen into the well, opened the door and went outside.

children.text: tadā sā dvāraṃ pidhāya madhye sthitā
children.translated_text: Then she closed the door and stood inside.

children.text: so 'pi ca bahiḥ sthito hā priye evaṃ vadanmahatā śabdena goditum ārabdhaḥ
children.translated_text: He too, standing outside and saying "Alas, beloved!", began to cry out loudly.

children.text: sāpi vigopakabhayād bahirnirgatya patiṃ madhye nināya
children.translated_text: She too, fearing public disgrace, came out, brought her husband inside,
and then the pair made a mutual agreement:

children.text: yadadyaprabhṛti mayā tvayā visaṃvādo na vidheyaḥ
children.translated_text: "From today onward neither I nor you shall create a quarrel."
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: anyadā sā hasantī narāntaragamanāya śukaṃ pṛcchati
children.translated_text: On another day, laughing, she asked the parrot about going to another man.

children.text: śuka āha yadeva manaso 'bhīṣṭaṃ tadeva kāryam
children.translated_text: The parrot said, "Whatever is desired by the mind, that should indeed be done.
And it has been said:
One should place a foot purified by sight; one should drink water purified by cloth.
One should speak a statement purified by truth; one should do what is purified by the mind.
Let them do what is agreeable to the mind, slender one; sorrow has come to you.

children.text: soḍhuṃ śaktāstathā vaktuṃ guṇāḍhyo brāhmaṇo yathā ||
children.translated_text: They are able to endure it and also to speak, as the virtuous Brahmin was."
<s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked, "How was that?"
The parrot said, "There is a city named <s>Viśālā</s>.
There was a sacrificing Brahmin there.

children.text: tasya patnī pāhinī nāma surūpā ativallabhā
children.translated_text: His wife, named <s>Pāhinī</s>, was beautiful and very dear to him.
Their son was made to learn all the sciences in due order by his father.

children.text: anyadā sa pitarau muktvā deśāntaraṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: One day, leaving his parents, he went to another country.
He became renowned as <s>Guṇāḍhya</s>.
And in the city of <s>Jayantī</s> he considered how to make a living by his intelligence.
Then he fed an ox with barley, grass, and the like.
That ox too wandered along after him.

children.text: anyadā sabandhanaṃ ṣaṇḍaṃ vidhāya vaṇijārakaveṣadhārī madanāyā veśyāyāḥ kuṭṭinīṃ jagāda asmadīyā balīvardāḥ savastukā prātareṣyanti
children.translated_text: One day, after tying up the ox, he put on the disguise of a merchant's servant and said to the procuress of the courtesan <s>Madanā</s>, "Our loaded bullocks will arrive in the morning.
Today I have come for the purpose of bringing grass.

children.text: tadyatra asmadīyasya balīvardasya sthānaṃ bhavati tatrāhaṃ svapimi
children.translated_text: So wherever there is a place for our bullock, there I shall sleep."

children.text: ityukte sā kuṭṭinī balīvardadhanaiṣiṇī taṃ sthāpayāmāsa
children.translated_text: When this was said, the procuress, eager for the wealth from the bullocks, let him stay.

children.text: so 'pi taṃ ṣaṇḍaṃ baddhvā vilāsinīpārśve yayau
children.translated_text: He too tied up that ox and went to the side of the courtesan.

children.text: tayā ca snāpito bhojitaśca guṇāḍhyo rajanyāṃ śṛṅgāritaḥ tatsakāśe sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Guṇāḍhya</s>, having been bathed, fed, and adorned by her at night, stayed near her.

children.text: so 'pi ca prabhātāyāṃ niśi prathamamevotthāya svarṇaśṛṅkhalā gṛhītvā jagāma
children.translated_text: And when the night had become dawn, he arose first, took a golden chain, and went away.

children.text: gate ca tasmin ekā ceṭī utthitā ṣaṇḍamadṛṣṭvā kuṭṭinīṃ pratyāha āue kimidam
children.translated_text: When he had gone, a maidservant got up, did not see the ox, and said to the procuress, "Ah! What is this?"

children.text: tatastaṃ vilāsinīpārśvādgataṃ jñātvā maunaṃ vidhāya sthitā
children.translated_text: Then, knowing that he had gone from the side of the courtesan, she remained silent.
And it has been said:
Loss of wealth, mental anguish, misconduct in the house,
deception and humiliation too: a wise man should not make these public.

children.text: anyadā guṇāḍhyo dyūtanirjitaḥ khaṭikāhasto veśyayā dhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: On another occasion <s>Guṇāḍhya</s>, defeated at gambling, was held by a courtesan, with chalk in his hand.
He thought of a stratagem and said, "<s>Śambala</s>, <s>Śambalī</s>!"
Then she released him out of fear of the king.

children.text: tatastasyāṃ calitāyāṃ pṛṣṭhalagna eva śambalīti vadan gacchati
children.translated_text: Then, when she had set out, he followed close behind her, saying, "<s>Śambalī</s>!"

children.text: tatastayā vijane nītvā hastātprasādya svarṇābharaṇaṃ dattam
children.translated_text: Then she led him to a secluded place, appeased him by the hand, and gave him a golden ornament.

children.text: soḍhuṃ tyaktuṃ ca yaḥ śakto manasā kṛtamanyathā
children.translated_text: One who is able to endure and to abandon what the mind has judged otherwise,

children.text: mano'nukūlatāṃ kurvanna sa nindyaḥ sadā satām ||
children.translated_text: while making himself agreeable to the mind, is never censured by good people.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
On another day, when she had set out, the parrot said:

children.text: gaccha devi na te deṣo gacchantyāḥ paraveśmani
children.translated_text: Go, lady; there is no fault in you as you go to another man's house,
if there is any intelligence in your body, as in the case of the mustard thief.
There is a city named <s>Śubhasthāna</s>.
There a merchant named <s>Daridra</s> lived.
A thief entered his house.

children.text: so 'pi ca tatrānyatkimapyalabhamānaḥ sarṣapān gṛhītvā nirgato rājapuruṣaiḥ prāptaḥ
children.translated_text: But he too, finding nothing else there, took mustard seeds and went out; he was caught by the king's men.

children.text: sarṣapān gale baddhvā bhrāmito rājakulātsa kathaṃ mucyate
children.translated_text: With the mustard seeds tied around his neck, he was paraded from the royal court. How is he to be freed?

children.text: uttaram yo yaḥ pṛcchati tasya tasyāgre vadati aho sarṣapāṇāṃ madhye na kiṃcit
children.translated_text: The answer: whoever asked him, before each one he said, "Ah, among the mustard seeds there is nothing at all."

children.text: tato rājñā sabhāyāmākārya pṛṣṭaḥ tava vaco'bhiprāyaṃ na jāne
children.translated_text: Then the king summoned him into the assembly and asked, "I do not understand the intention of your speech."
He said, "On the yearly day of <s>Bali</s>, people tie five protecting mustard seeds
on their hands; surely, beyond this, that is no valid proof."

children.text: yato 'hametāvadbhirapi gale baddhairbaddhaḥ rājāpi tadākarṇya hasaṃstaṃ mumoca
children.translated_text: "For I have been bound even with so many of them tied around my neck." The king too, hearing that, laughed and released him.
Having heard this, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
On another day <s>Prabhāvatī</s> set out.

children.text: śukaḥ prāha kuru yadrocate bhīru yadi kartuṃ tvamīśvarā
children.translated_text: The parrot said, "Do what pleases you, timid one, if you are capable of doing it,

children.text: yathā santikayā bhartā svacchandā ca vimocitā ||
children.translated_text: as <s>Santikā</s> freed both her husband and <s>Svacchandā</s>."
There is a city called <s>Karahaḍa</s>.
There the king, rightly named, was called <s>Guṇapriya</s>.
And there was a guild-merchant named <s>Soḍhaka</s>.
His wife, named <s>Santikā</s>, was devoted to her husband.
There too was another merchant.
His wife, named <s>Svacchandā</s>, was unchaste.

children.text: sā ca soḍhākaṃ nityamicchati paraṃ so 'bhivāñchāṃ na vidhatte
children.translated_text: She constantly desired <s>Soḍhaka</s>, but he did not grant her wish.

children.text: anyadā ca manorathābhidhaṃ yakṣaṃ namaskartuṃ jagāma saḥ
children.translated_text: One day he went to pay homage to a <s>yakṣa</s> named <s>Manoratha</s>.
Then <s>Svacchandā</s>, following behind him, entered there.
And he, made favorable by her gestures and expressions, enjoyed her.
And it is rightly said:

children.text: sanmārge tāvadāste prabhavati puruṣastāvadevendriyāṇāṃ lajjāṃ tāvadvidhatte vinayamapi samālambate tāvadeva
children.translated_text: A man remains on the good path only so long as he has mastery over his senses; only so long does he observe modesty and take hold of discipline.

children.text: bhrūcāpākṛṣṭamuktāḥ śravaṇapathajuṣo nīlapakṣmāṇa ete yāvallīlāvatīnāṃ na hṛdi dhṛtimuṣo dṛṣṭibāṇāḥ patanti ||
children.translated_text: Until the arrow-glances of graceful women, released from the drawn bow of their brows, dark-lashed and reaching the path of the ear, fall into the heart and steal away firmness.

children.text: tacca mithunaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājapuruṣaḥ tadbandhanāya yakṣagṛhaṃ veṣṭitam
children.translated_text: Seeing that couple, a royal officer surrounded the <s>yakṣa</s> shrine in order to arrest them.

children.text: santikā ca śuddhiṃ jñātvā rātrau mahatā tūryaśabdena yakṣagṛhaṃ gatā
children.translated_text: And <s>Santikā</s>, knowing the truth, went at night to the <s>yakṣa</s> shrine with a great sound of instruments.

children.text: teṣāmārakṣakāṇāṃ purata uktam ahamadyadinavratā yakṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhojanaṃ vijane vidhāsye
children.translated_text: In front of those guards she said, "Today I am keeping a daytime vow; after seeing the <s>yakṣa</s>, I shall take food in private.

children.text: māṃ ca kiṃciddhanaṃ gṛhītvā madhye praveśayatu
children.translated_text: Let someone take a little money from me and let me enter inside."
They did exactly so.
Then she made <s>Svacchandā</s> put on her own clothes and sent her outside.
She herself remained inside.

children.text: taṃ ca prātarnijakāntāsahitaṃ dṛṣṭvā ārakṣakā vilakṣībabhūvuḥ
children.translated_text: And when in the morning the guards saw him together with his own wife, they were embarrassed.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
On another day <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot.

children.text: śukaḥ prāha gaccha devi mano yatra ramate te narāntare
children.translated_text: The parrot said, "Go, lady, where your mind delights in another man,
if, like <s>Kelikā</s>, you know the wondrous deception of a husband.

children.text: asti sābhramatyā nadyāstaṭe śaṅkhapuraṃ nāma sthānam
children.translated_text: On the bank of the river <s>Sābhramatī</s> there is a place named <s>Śaṅkhapura</s>.
And there was a wealthy farmer named <s>Sūra</s>.

children.text: tasya kelikā bhāryā paraṃ kuṭilā kulaṭā ca
children.translated_text: His wife <s>Kelikā</s> was extremely crooked and unchaste.
She desired a Brahmin who lived in <s>Siddheśvarapura</s> on the other bank of the river.

children.text: tadāsaktā ca rātrau prātiveśikādūtikāsāhāyyānnadīṃ tīrtvā tadantikaṃ prāpnoti
children.translated_text: Attached to him, at night with the help of a neighboring female messenger she crossed the river and reached his side.
One day her husband found out.
And he went there to investigate her conduct.

children.text: yāvatsā nadītīre tatra samāgatā tayā ca tāvaddṛṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as she arrived there on the riverbank, she saw him.

children.text: tatastaraṇaghaṭaṃ pānīyabhṛtaṃ vidhāya prātiveśmikāgṛhamadhye bhaṭṭārikāṃ maṇḍayitvā tena payasā snāpayitvā pratyuvāca prathamasaṃketitāṃ dūtikāmuddiśya svāmini purā tvayā uktaṃ yadi tvaṃ siddheśvarīṃ na snāpayasi tataḥ pañcānāṃ dinānāṃ madhye tvadbhartṛbharaṇaṃ bhaviṣyati tato yadi tvadvacanapramāṇaṃ tadā mama patiściraṃ jīvatu
children.translated_text: Then, taking the crossing-pot filled with water, she set up the goddess in the neighbor's house, bathed her with that water, and said in reply, addressing the messenger who had been signaled beforehand: "Mistress, earlier you said, 'If you do not bathe <s>Siddheśvarī</s>, then within five days there will be the death of your husband.' Therefore, if your word is true, may my husband live long."

children.text: prātiveśmikayoktam evamastviti śrutvā patistuṣṭo bhūtvālakṣita eva jagāma
children.translated_text: The neighbor woman said, "So be it." Hearing this, the husband became pleased and went away unnoticed.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
On another day, when <s>Prabhāvatī</s> had asked, the parrot said:

children.text: vraja devi na doṣo 'sti vrajatāṃ sarvakarmasu
children.translated_text: Go, lady; there is no fault in any actions of those who go,
when they possess intelligence as their helper, as <s>Mandodarī</s> did.
<s>Prabhāvatī</s> said, "How is this?"
The parrot said: There is a city named <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>.
There a king named <s>Hemaprabha</s> lived.
His minister was <s>Śrutaśīla</s>.
There was a merchant named <s>Yaśodhara</s>.
His wife was <s>Mohinī</s>.
Their daughter was <s>Mandodarī</s>.
She was given to the merchant <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, who had come to <s>Kāntipurī</s>.
That couple was exceedingly attached and given over to love.

children.text: sā ca prātiveśmikayā pitṛbhāryayā kuṭṭinyā daṃṣṭrākarālayā yojitamanyaṃ rājaputram upabhuṅkte
children.translated_text: But she, being brought together by a neighboring procuress, her father's wife, who was terrible with her fangs, enjoyed another man, a prince.

children.text: sāpannasattvā bhūtā garbhasaṃbhavātsaṃjāte dohade rājavallabhaṃ mayūraṃ mārayitvā bhakṣitavatī
children.translated_text: When she became pregnant and a craving arose from the pregnancy, she had the king's favorite peacock killed and ate it.

children.text: rājā tu tasminmayūre samāgate bhuṅkte iti sthitiḥ
children.translated_text: Now the rule was that when that peacock came, the king would eat.
But on that day, at mealtime, it was not found.
When a drum proclamation was made, the procuress touched the drum.

children.text: tayā ca jñātaṃ yatkayācidāpannasattvayā mayūro dohadādbhakṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: And she understood that some pregnant woman had eaten the peacock because of a pregnancy-craving.

children.text: tataḥ sā garbhavatī pṛṣṭā tayā kuṭṭinī gṛhamāgatā saṃmānitā
children.translated_text: Then that pregnant woman was questioned, and the procuress came to her house and was honored by her.
And it has been said:

children.text: mādhuryaṃ pramadājane sulalitaṃ dākṣiṇyamārye jane śauryaṃ śatruṣu mārdavaṃ gurujane dharmiṣṭhatā sādhuṣu
children.translated_text: Sweetness toward women, graceful courtesy toward noble people, valor toward enemies, gentleness toward elders, righteousness toward the good,

children.text: marmajñeṣvanuvartanaṃ bahuvidhaṃ mānaṃ jane garvite śāṭhyaṃ pāpajane narasya kathitāḥ paryantamaṣṭau guṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: varied compliance toward those who know one's weak points, respect toward the proud, and deceit toward wicked people: these are said to be the eight qualities of a man at the limit.
And the whole affair of the peacock was reported by her.
But that procuress was a betrayer of trust.
And it has been said:
One should not trust the untrustworthy; even one who is trusted should not be trusted too far.
Danger born from trust cuts one off even from the root.

children.text: dāreṣu gopyaṃ puruṣasya kiṃcidgopyaṃ vayasyeṣu suteṣu kiṃcit
children.translated_text: A man should conceal some things from his wife, some from friends, and some from sons.

children.text: yuktaṃ na yuktaṃ manasā vicintya vadedvipaścinmahato 'nurodhāt ||
children.translated_text: Having considered in his mind what is proper and improper, the wise man should speak out of regard for the great.
Moreover:
Here one should observe the courteous words of enemies.
Deer that do not consider the meaning of a song go to ruin.
It is also said in the <s>Kirāta</s>:

children.text: vrajanti te mūḍhadhiyaḥ parābhavaṃ bhavanti māyāviṣu ye na māyinaḥ
children.translated_text: Those dull-witted people go to defeat who are not deceitful toward the deceitful.

children.text: praviśya hi ghnanti śaṭhāstathāvidhān asaṃvṛtāṅgān niśitā iveṣavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For rogues enter and strike such people, whose bodies are uncovered, like sharp arrows.
When the procuress had learned all that, it was reported to the minister.
And by the minister also to the king.
The king said:

children.text: mā hohi suhaggāhi mā pattihi jaṃ ṇa diṭṭhapaccakkhaṃ
children.translated_text: Do not be easily convinced; do not believe what has not been seen directly.
Even when it has been seen directly, know what is proper and improper.

children.text: mā bhava sukhagrāhī mā pratyehi yanna dṛṣṭaṃ pratyakṣam
children.translated_text: Do not be one who grasps at ease; do not trust what has not been seen with direct perception.
Even when something has been directly seen, discern what is proper and improper.
Such a deed cannot be carried out by the wife of the chief merchant of the city.

children.text: yāvadātmanā na dṛṣṭaṃ tāvadasau na viḍambyaḥ
children.translated_text: So long as it has not been seen by oneself, she must not be disgraced.
And this was reported by the minister in front of the procuress.

children.text: kuṭṭinī ca mantriṇaṃ peṭāyāṃ nikṣipya tadgṛhe nyāsavyājena mumoca
children.translated_text: The procuress put the minister into a chest and, under the pretext of a deposit, left it in that house.

children.text: svayaṃ ca tatra gatvā tāmabhāṣata mugdhe yanmayūrabhakṣaṇaṃ kṛtaṃ tattvaṃ me ślāghyā
children.translated_text: She herself went there and addressed the woman: 'Innocent girl, as for the eating of the peacock that you did, you are to be praised by me for that truth.'
And it has been said:

children.text: eṇaḥ kuraṅgo harimas tittirirlāva eva ca
children.translated_text: The antelope, the deer, the lion, the partridge, and the quail,
and also the peacock, the spotted deer, and the tortoise are excellent even among classes of meat.
Again the whole event was asked about.
And as it was being told, the minister heard it through the signal made by striking the chest.
How, then, could that merchant's wife, her father, and her father-in-law be released?
And it has been said:
A man does not see good things from association with low people.
For a villain displays only distortion even toward one who is very dear.

children.text: nāśayitumeva nīcaḥ parakāryaṃ vetti na prasādhayitum
children.translated_text: A low man knows how to ruin another's work, not how to accomplish it.
The power of a fingernail is only to tear; it cannot pull out what is not pierced.

children.text: dujjaṇajaṇaṇaṃ sagge kāaccāo vi hoi vibuhāṇaṃ
children.translated_text: In the company of wicked people, even the wise in heaven may suffer bodily destruction.

children.text: pecchaha tilehi pattaṃ khalasaṃge pīḍaṇaṃ jatto ||
children.translated_text: Look: because of association with a villain, even sesame seeds undergo crushing.
In the company of wicked people, even the wise may give up the body.
Behold: even sesame seeds undergo pressing because of association with what is base.

children.text: yāvatsā kuṭṭinī peṭāṃ hastena hanti tāvatsā vaṇikputrī savitarkamavādīt
children.translated_text: As the procuress was striking the chest with her hand, that merchant's daughter spoke with suspicion:
'The night has dawned only as long as this was done by me;
and when I awoke then, mother, nothing further was seen before me.'
'Mother, I saw such a dream.

children.text: yaḥ kaścidarthapramāṇo me bhavati sa kathyatām
children.translated_text: Whatever meaning it has for me, let that be told.'
Having heard this, the minister struck the door and came out.

children.text: tataḥ saṃmānitā vaṇigvadhūḥ sā tu kuṭṭinīti nirvāsitā
children.translated_text: Then the merchant's wife was honored, but that procuress was banished.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
Again, when questioned by <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, the parrot said:
'Go, lady, go again; such is my opinion,
if you know some reply, as was done by <s>Māḍhukā</s>.'
Hearing that, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> said, 'How was that?'

children.text: śukaḥ prāha dāmbhilāgrāme soḍhāko nāma karṣukaḥ
children.translated_text: The parrot said: In the village of <s>Dāmbhilā</s> there was a farmer named <s>Soḍhāka</s>.
His wife was named <s>Māḍhukā</s>.

children.text: tāṃ ca bhaktahāriṇīṃ pathi gacchantīm eko bahiḥ sūrapālākhyo naro bhuṅkte
children.translated_text: As she was going along the road carrying cooked rice, a certain man outside, named <s>Sūrapāla</s>, enjoyed her.

children.text: sā kadācinmārge bhaktaṃ muktvā tena saha sthitā
children.translated_text: Once, having put down the rice on the road, she stayed with him.

children.text: tato mūladevena dhūrtena tasminbhakte uṣṭrikā kṛtā
children.translated_text: Then the rogue <s>Mūladeva</s> turned that food into a she-camel.

children.text: tayā ca evaṃ jātaṃ bhaktam anutpāṭayitvā nīnam
children.translated_text: And when the food had become like that, she led it away without lifting it up.

children.text: yāvacca bhartrā uṣṭrikā dṛṣṭā tāvatkimidamiti sā pṛṣṭā
children.translated_text: And when her husband saw the she-camel, he asked her, 'What is this?'

children.text: tatastayā tatkālottaraṃ kṛtvoktaṃ nātha adya rātrau svapne uṣṭrikayā bhakṣito dṛṣṭastvam
children.translated_text: Then she immediately made a reply and said, "Lord, tonight in a dream I saw you being eaten by a she-camel.
Therefore I did this contrary act in order to remove the obstacle.
Eat without anxiety, so that the obstacle may perish."
Hearing this, he, whose mind was absorbed in passion, ate even the she-camel.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
On another day her friends spoke to her in this way, precisely to make her go to another man:

children.text: yatra svedalavairalaṃ vilulitairvyālupyate candanaṃ sacchedairmaṇitaiśca yatra raṇitaṃ na śrūyate nūpuram
children.translated_text: "Where sandal-paste is abundantly rubbed away by drops of sweat and loosened hair, where the anklet is not heard because of interrupted moans and cries,

children.text: yatrāyāntyacireṇa sarvaviṣayāḥ kāmaṃ tadekāgrataḥ sakhyastatsurataṃ bhaṇāmi rataye śeṣā ca lokasthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: where all the senses soon come to complete one-pointedness in desire, friends, that I call love-making for pleasure; the rest is merely the way of the world.
And likewise:

children.text: saṃsaatulaṇa jahiṃ caḍai tassuṇa jīviu dhaṇu
children.translated_text: When one does not mount the balance of doubt, his life is not blessed.

children.text: āi parā jahi lahijjai taṃ ji bhaṇijjii pemmu ||
children.translated_text: When another is obtained on arrival, that alone is called love.

children.text: saṃśayatulāyāṃ na yaḥ ārohati tasya na jīvitaṃ dhanyam
children.translated_text: For one who does not climb onto the balance of uncertainty, life is not blessed.

children.text: āgate parā yā labhyate tadeva bhaṇyate prema ||
children.translated_text: When, after coming, another is obtained, that indeed is called love.
Health, supreme joy, happiness, and enthusiasm,
lordship too, are all meaningless without union with the beloved.
And it has been said:
Seeing herself shining in the reflection of a mirror, her wide, unmoving eyes fixed there,

children.text: haropayāne tvaritā babhūva strīṇāṃ priyālokaphalo hi veṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: she hurried at <s>Hara</s>'s approach; for women's adornment bears fruit in the sight of the beloved.
The parrot said:
Men who always say what is pleasant, O king, are easy to find;

children.text: apriyasya tu pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: but a speaker and a hearer of what is unpleasant yet beneficial are hard to find.

children.text: tataḥ kiṃ bahunoktena tvaṃ caitāḥ kṛtyakovidāḥ
children.translated_text: So what need is there of many words? You and these women are skilled in action.
After hearing the conduct of the procuress, you should consider it, though you are in haste.
<s>Prabhāvatī</s> said, "How was this?"
The parrot said, "There is a city named <s>Padmāvatī</s>.
There, on roads paved with jewels, the expanse of the sun shines,
as if the red glow of the jewels on <s>Śeṣa</s>'s hoods had come down to the earth.
There was a king named <s>Sudarśana</s>.
By the moon, by <s>Hari</s>, by <s>Balin</s>, and by King <s>Kuśa</s>,
his fortune in the hare, power, stratagem, and generosity was not surpassed.
What can be said in praise of that king, who was devoted to protecting his subjects,

children.text: yasmiṃlloke na dṛṣṭā hi doṣā ravikarairiva ||
children.translated_text: in whose realm faults were not seen, just as they are not seen in the sun's rays?
His wife was named <s>Śṛṅgārasundarī</s>.
While that king was sporting with her, the summer season arrived.

children.text: yatra sūraḥ kharo ghasro yatra dīrgho 'tiduḥsahaḥ
children.translated_text: In it the sun is harsh, the day is harsh and long, and exceedingly hard to bear;

children.text: kharaśca pavano bhīru grīṣme sarvamidaṃ kharam ||
children.translated_text: the wind too is harsh, timid one; in summer all this is harsh.

children.text: candanaṃ śucivastraṃ ca pānīyaṃ śuci śītalam
children.translated_text: Sandal-paste, clean clothes, and pure, cool water
being enjoyed, the sweet and clean season triumphs, not otherwise.
For those who have sandal-paste at midday, bathing and refreshment in the evening,
and the breeze of fans at night, even summer is a servant.

children.text: evaṃvidhe grīṣme ca candranāmā vaṇik prabhāvatībhāryāsameto gṛhoparibhūmikāyām ārūḍhaḥ
children.translated_text: In such a summer a merchant named <s>Candra</s>, together with his wife <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, had gone up to the upper story of his house.
Though furnished with rays as hands, the supportless sun had gone to the shore of the western ocean.
And it has been said:

children.text: pratikūlatāmupagate hi vidhau viphalatvameti bahu sādhanatā
children.translated_text: When fate has turned hostile, an abundance of means comes to futility;
even the thousand rays of the lord of day did not serve as a support for him as he was about to fall.

children.text: tatrasthaḥ sa tathā bhānū rāgaśeṣo gatāṃśukaḥ
children.translated_text: Standing there, the sun, with only redness left and its rays gone,
shone like a coral jar slipped from the hand of the bride <s>Sandhyā</s>.
Meanwhile, wide-eyed one, the moon, intent on standing on the peak of the eastern mountain
and slaying the enemy darkness, rose surrounded by soldiers in the form of rays.
The moon shines at the face of the east, standing on the peak of the mountain of rising,
like a lamp for the three worlds covered by darkness.
Having climbed the mountain of rising, the moon shines at the beginning of night,
like the bride-price in the lap of the woman Night, set upon the black head.

children.text: evaṃvidhe niśāmukhe sa vaṇik vikrīḍitayā tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍitaḥ
children.translated_text: At such a beginning of night, that merchant sported together with her, who had been engaged in amorous play.
A son named <s>Rāma</s> was born to him.
His father had him taught all the sciences without remainder.

children.text: tasya mātānyadā candraṃ prāha mama eka eva putraḥ
children.translated_text: One day his mother said to <s>Candra</s>, "I have only one son.
Therefore I am excessively afflicted with sorrow."

children.text: candraḥ prāha eko 'pi tvadīyaḥ sutaḥ ślāghyaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Candra</s> said, "Even though he is only one, your son is praiseworthy.
And it has been said:
Clever, sweet-spoken, generous, profound, and a repository of arts,
and likewise appreciative of virtues: even one such excellent son is enough.
And likewise:
What use are many sons who bring grief and burning pain?
Better one who supports the family, through whom the family becomes renowned.

children.text: ityuktvā dhūrtamāyāṃ kuṭṭinīmākāryedamabravīt tava kanakasahasraṃ dāsye
children.translated_text: Having said this, he summoned a procuress named <s>Dhūrtamāyā</s> and said, "I will give you a thousand pieces of gold.
Make my son skilled in cheating by women's wiles."

children.text: tatheti tayā pratijñāte putraṃ samākṣikaṃ tasyai dattvā yadyasmatputraḥ kvāpi veśyāyāḥ kapaṭena jito bhavati tadāhaṃ dviguṇaṃ kanakaṃ grahīṣye
children.translated_text: When she had promised, "So be it," he handed his son over to her in the presence of witnesses, saying, "If our son is ever defeated by the deceit of a courtesan, then I shall take twice the gold."
She said, "So be it."
After having this put in writing, he sent his son to her house.
Staying there, he learned the distortions that arise among courtesans.
For example:
the artificial speech of courtesans, false oaths as well,

children.text: kauṭilyaṃ kṛtrimaṃ bhāvaṃ kṛtrimaṃ ruditaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: crookedness, feigned emotion, and feigned weeping too;

children.text: hāsyaṃ ca kṛtrimaṃ duḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ caivamapārthakam
children.translated_text: artificial laughter, artificial sorrow, and similarly baseless happiness;
petitioning accompanied by humility, an appearance of affection, freedom from desire;
equanimity in pleasure and pain, and treating <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> alike.
And also the display of crooked procedure before serpents.
And likewise:

children.text: aharaṃ karaṃ kavolaṃ thaṇajualaṃ ṇāhimaṇḍalaṃ ramaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: The lip, the hand, the cheek, the pair of breasts, the circle of the navel, the lover,

children.text: itthiajaṇasāmaṇṇaṃ hiaaṃ jaṃ jassa taṃ tassa
children.translated_text: are common to women; the heart belongs to the one to whom it belongs.

children.text: adharaḥ karaḥ kapolaḥ stanayugalaṃ nābhimaṇḍalaṃ ramaṇam
children.translated_text: The lower lip, the hand, the cheek, the pair of breasts, the circle of the navel, and the lover

children.text: strījanasāmānyaṃ hṛdayaṃ yad yasyās tat tasyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are common to womankind; but the heart, whatever woman's it is, is hers alone.
Thus he had been taught the whole conduct connected with courtesans and the like.

children.text: tataḥ sa putraḥ pratijñāpūrvaṃ vaṇije samarpitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that son was entrusted to the merchant after an undertaking had been made.
And, at his father's command, he was sent to <s>Suvarṇadvīpa</s> for trade.
There was a courtesan named <s>Kalāvatī</s> there.
He stayed with her for one year.

children.text: tāṃ vaiśikāni kurvantīṃ sa prāha viśeṣaṃ vada
children.translated_text: When she was practicing courtesan's arts, he said to her, "Tell me something special."
"Even my younger sister says this to me."

children.text: tato bahubhirapi vaiśikairna tatsarvasvaṃ gṛhītuṃ śaknoti
children.translated_text: Thus, even with many courtesan's tricks, she was unable to take all his property.
Then she reported everything to her mother.
Her mother too said, "Certainly this man is a courtesan's son."
"He cannot be seized by such methods."
"He must be seized only by stratagem."

children.text: tato yadāyaṃ svadeśaṃ gantukāmastvām utkalāpayati tadā tvayā vācyam ahamapi tatra yāsyāmi
children.translated_text: "So when he, wishing to go to his own country, urges you to get up, then you must say, 'I too shall go there.'"

children.text: yadi na nayasi tadā mariṣyāmītyuktvā kūpe jhampā deyā
children.translated_text: "If you do not take me, then, saying 'I shall die,' you must throw yourself into the well."
"Then, out of affection, he will give you everything."
She said, "Mother, what use is his wealth to me without him?"
And it has been said:
Those gains that come with excessive hardship and with transgression of <s>dharma</s> (right conduct),

children.text: śatrūṇāṃ praṇipātena mā sma teṣu manaḥ kṛthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: or through bowing down before enemies, do not set your mind on them.

children.text: mātā āha bhīru mā maivaṃ vada
children.translated_text: The mother said, "Timid girl, do not speak so."
"Wealth brings death, and it also preserves life."
And it has been said:
Without taking hold of daring, a man does not see good fortune.
The daring person, in every undertaking, is the best vessel of <s>Lakṣmī</s>.
Without piercing others' vital points, without doing a deed difficult to do,
without striking, like a fisherman, one does not obtain great prosperity.
Time makes even and uneven; time produces humiliation and honor.

children.text: kālaḥ karoti puruṣaṃ dātāraṃ yācitāraṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Time makes a man both a giver and a beggar.
"And I shall arrange a net down there."

children.text: iti kuṭṭinīvacanam ākarṇya tayā tathā kṛtat
children.translated_text: Having heard the procuress's words, she did just that.

children.text: tathā ca kṛte tena sarvasvaṃ dattam
children.translated_text: And when she had done so, he gave everything to her.

children.text: koṭisaṃkhyaṃ ca dravyaṃ gṛhītvā mānarahito niṣkāsitaḥ
children.translated_text: After taking wealth numbered by crores, she expelled him, stripped of honor.
And it has been said:

children.text: vesā vi ramanti jaṇaṃ piaṃ pi vañcanti atthaloheṇa
children.translated_text: Courtesans indeed enjoy a man, and even a beloved one they deceive from greed for money.

children.text: tāṇa ṇamo vesāṇaṃ appā vi ṇa vallaho jāṇa
children.translated_text: Homage to those courtesans for whom even their own self is not dear.

children.text: veśyā api ramante janaṃ priyamapi vañcayanti arthalobhena
children.translated_text: Courtesans indeed enjoy a man, and even a beloved one they deceive from greed for wealth.

children.text: tābhyo namo veśyābhyaḥ ātmāpi na vallabho yāsām ||
children.translated_text: Homage to those courtesans for whom even the self is not dear.

children.text: sa ca tathā dhanamānaparibhavaṃ prāpitaḥ parapotamāruhya svagṛhamāgamat
children.translated_text: Thus brought to loss of wealth and honor, he boarded another ship and came home.

children.text: ekākinaṃ sutaṃ dhanaparijanavarjitaṃ dṛṣṭvā pitā sabāṣpaṃ dhanakṣayakāraṇaṃ pṛcchati
children.translated_text: Seeing his son alone, without wealth or attendants, his father, with tears in his eyes, asked the cause of the loss of wealth.
He too, ashamed himself, reported it through the mouth of the family minister.
His father said, "Child, do not give way to grief."
"For men, misfortunes also become fortunes."
And it has been said:
Why do you bear this anxiety, lord of elephant herds, your pair of eyes closed because of separation from the herd?

children.text: piṇḍaṃ gṛhāṇa piṣa vāri yathopanītaṃ daivādbhavanti vipadaḥ kila sampado vā ||
children.translated_text: Take the lump of food, drink the water as brought; by fate, surely, misfortunes or fortunes come to pass.
What is the use of this wealth, which passes quickly, for high-minded men?

children.text: gatena jāyate khedo darpaś caivāgatena ca ||
children.translated_text: When it is gone, sorrow arises, and when it has come, pride as well.

children.text: evaṃ sutaṃ samāśvāsya dhūrtamāyāmākārya idamabravīt śṛṇu yadatra kautukaṃ saṃvṛttam
children.translated_text: Having thus consoled his son, he summoned <s>Dhūrtamāyā</s> and said this: "Listen to the curious thing that happened here."
"Although my son stayed with you, he came back having lost all his property."
She said, "Who has not been broken by women?"
And it has been said:

children.text: ko 'rthānprāpya na garvito viṣayiṇaḥ kasyāpado 'staṃ gatāḥ strībhiḥ kasya na khaṇḍitaṃ bhuvi manaḥ ko nāma rājñāṃ priyaḥ
children.translated_text: Who, having obtained wealth, has not become proud? For what sensual man have calamities ceased? Whose mind on earth has not been broken by women? Who indeed is dear to kings?

children.text: kaḥ kālasya na gocarāntaragataḥ ko 'rthī gato gauravaṃ ko vā durjanavāgurāsu patitaḥ kṣemeṇa yātaḥ pumān ||
children.translated_text: Who has not entered the range of Time? What petitioner has gained dignity? What man, fallen into the snares of the wicked, has gone away safely?
In the space between the fire of passion, in a dense thicket of trees bright with bristling hair,
<s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Govinda</s> too have been mocked by the thief <s>Madana</s>.
In the space within the flame of love, in the very dense thicket of trees adorned with rolling hair,
<s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, <s>Nara</s>, and <s>Govinda</s> have been made sport of by the thief <s>Madana</s>.

children.text: tattvaṃ punaḥ potaṃ bhṛtaṃ kṛtvā māṃ putrānvitāṃ tatra preṣaya
children.translated_text: "Therefore load a ship again and send me there together with your son."
And it has been said:
For a deed done one should do a counter-deed; for injury, counter-injury.

children.text: tvayā luñcāpitāḥ pakṣā mayā luñcāpitaṃ śiraḥ ||
children.translated_text: You had my wings plucked; I had your head plucked.

children.text: mayāpyuktaṃ yadi tvadīyaputraḥ kvāpi striyā vañcyate tadā mama dūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: I too said, "If your son is deceived anywhere by a woman, then the fault is mine."
And it has been said:
Though this earth is supported by the elephants of the quarters, the tortoise, the family mountains, and the lord of serpents, it may move;
but the undertaking of men of stainless mind does not move, even at the end of an age.
And likewise:

children.text: acalā calanti palae majjāaṃ sāarā vilaṅghanti
children.translated_text: Mountains move at dissolution; the oceans overstep their boundaries.

children.text: karuā vi taha vikāle paḍivaṇṇa sādha siḍhilenti ||
children.translated_text: Even weighty people, in such a bad time, do not loosen the task they have undertaken.
The immovable mountains move at the dissolution; the oceans overstep their bounds.

children.text: gurukā api tathā vikāle pratipannasādhanaṃ na śithilayanti ||
children.translated_text: Even the weighty, likewise in an adverse time, do not slacken the means they have undertaken.

children.text: dhīrā jāṇa pamāṇaṃ jimiavve taha vi jaṃpiavve a
children.translated_text: The steadfast know the measure in eating, and likewise in speaking;
things overeaten and overspoken, child, are afterward regretted, not before.

children.text: dhīrā jānanti pramāṇaṃ jemanasya tathāpi kathanasya ca
children.translated_text: Steady people know the measure of eating and also of speaking;

children.text: api bhuktaṃ jalpitaṃ paścād vatse na tapyanti ||
children.translated_text: after eating and speaking, child, they do not suffer regret.

children.text: tataḥ śreṣṭhī taṃ putraṃ preṣayāmāsāśu tayā samaṃ suvarṇadvīpe
children.translated_text: Then the merchant quickly sent that son together with her to <s>Suvarṇadvīpa</s>.
Then all the townspeople there became pleased with him.

children.text: sā ca kalāvatī sānukūlā taṃ vinayenājuhāva
children.translated_text: And that <s>Kalāvatī</s>, favorably disposed, summoned him with courtesy.

children.text: tathā ca sa tayāvarjito yathāsau ātmāyattaḥ kṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: And he was so won over by her that he was made dependent on her.
And all his wealth was taken.

children.text: tataḥ sā dhūrtamāyā kuṭṭinī kiṃ karotu iti praśnaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the question was: what should the procuress <s>Dhūrtamāyā</s> do?
She said, "Parrot, I do not know.
You tell me."

children.text: śukaḥ yadyadya na yāsi tadā kathayāmi
children.translated_text: The parrot said, "If you do not go today, then I shall tell you."
She said, "I shall not go."

children.text: śukaḥ yadā tasya sarvaṃ gṛhītam tasminsamaye kaiściddinaiścāgre 'pi cāṇḍālarūpadhāriṇī dhūrtamāyā nityaṃ nityaṃ gaveṣamāṇaiva kiṃcit
children.translated_text: The parrot said, "When all his property had been taken, at that time, after some days had passed, <s>Dhūrtamāyā</s>, wearing the appearance of a <s>cāṇḍāla</s> woman, was constantly searching for something.

children.text: anyadā sa kalāvatyā sahitaḥ khaṭvāyāmupaviṣṭastayā dṛṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: One day she saw him seated on a bed together with <s>Kalāvatī</s>.

children.text: tā dvāri dṛṣṭvā sahasotthāya nāśayitumudyataḥ pūrvameva saṃketitam
children.translated_text: Seeing her at the door, he suddenly rose, intending to run away, as had already been arranged.
As he rose, <s>Kalāvatī</s> too rose after him.
And she said, "What is this?"
<s>Rāma</s> said to her, "Good lady, this is my mother.

children.text: ahaṃ ca hṛtārthako bahudinebhyo na tayā dṛṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: I have lost my wealth, and she has not seen me for many days."

children.text: dhūrtamāyāpi taṃ saṃketasthaṃ dvārasthaiva saśaṅkā hastasaṃjñayā ājuhāva
children.translated_text: <s>Dhūrtamāyā</s> too, standing at the doorway according to the arrangement, anxiously summoned him with a gesture of the hand.
"Wake up! After a long time I have found you, gone into a courtesan's house.

children.text: mlecchībhūtā iyaṃ veśyā sarvasvaṃ me tvayā hṛtam ||
children.translated_text: This courtesan has turned you into a barbarian; all my property has been carried off by you."

children.text: yāvadevaṃ gṛhāṅgaṇagatā śapati tāvatsa vaṇik cāṇḍālarūpī samāgatya tatpādayoḥ patitaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as she was cursing him in this way in the courtyard of the house, that merchant, disguised as a <s>cāṇḍāla</s>, came up and fell at her feet.

children.text: etacca dṛṣṭvā kalāvatī kuṭṭinīsahitā tām gṛhamadhye nītvā pṛcchati sma amba ko 'yam kiṃ jātīyaḥ tvaṃ kā tayoktam padmāvatīpurīnāthasya rājñaḥ sudarśanasya mātaṅgī gāyinī aham
children.translated_text: Seeing this, <s>Kalāvatī</s>, together with the procuress, led her into the house and asked, "Mother, who is this man? Of what caste is he? Who are you?" She replied, "I am a <s>mātaṅgī</s> singer of King <s>Sudarśana</s>, lord of <s>Padmāvatīpurī</s>.

children.text: ayaṃ ca madīyaṃ dravyaṃ hṛtvā ihāgataḥ
children.translated_text: And this man stole my property and came here.
And that has been obtained by you.
I have learned this; but now let him come here."

children.text: tataḥ kuṭṭinī kalāvatāsahitā tatpādayorlagnā uvāca gṛhāṇedaṃ dravyam
children.translated_text: Then the procuress, together with <s>Kalāvatī</s>, clung to her feet and said, "Take this property."
<s>Dhūrtamāyā</s> said, "I will not take it in a corner of the house.
I will take it with the king knowing of it."

children.text: tato veśyāmātāpi atiśayena bhītā mātaṅgīṃ pratijagāda imāṃ matsutāṃ rakṣa rakṣa
children.translated_text: Then the courtesan's mother, exceedingly frightened, answered the <s>mātaṅgī</s>, "Protect, protect this daughter of mine.

children.text: pāramparyāgataṃ dravyaṃ gṛhāṇa sarvasvam paraṃ māṃ maivaṃ viḍambaya
children.translated_text: Take the wealth that has come down through the family, everything we own, but do not disgrace me in this way."
<s>Dhūrtamāyā</s> said, "I will take it."

children.text: tataḥ sā veśyayā kuṭṭinyā saha hastapādau gṛhītvā saṃmānitā
children.translated_text: Then she was honored by the courtesan and the procuress, who took hold of her hands and feet.

children.text: dhūrtamāyāpi nijaṃ tadīyaṃ dravyaṃ sarvasvaṃ ca gṛhītvā rāmeṇa saha potamāruhya svagṛhamāgatya mahotsavamakārayat
children.translated_text: <s>Dhūrtamāyā</s>, having taken her own and his wealth, and indeed all of it, boarded a ship with <s>Rāma</s>, came to her own house, and held a great celebration.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
Then on another day <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot.
The parrot too said,
"Go, lady, if, when you are with a lover, you know how,
like <s>Sajjanī</s> of old, to speak before your husband when he has seized your hair."
<s>Prabhāvatī</s> said, "What is this?"
The parrot said, "There is a city named <s>Candrapura</s>.
There lived a wealthy carpenter named <s>Sūrapāla</s>.

children.text: tasya sajjanī nāma bhāryā atyantaṃ parapuruṣalampaṭā
children.translated_text: His wife, named <s>Sajjanī</s>, was extremely fond of other men.

children.text: tāṃ ca tadgṛhasthāṃ devako nāma ramate
children.translated_text: And, while she was in that house, a man named <s>Devaka</s> enjoyed her.

children.text: iti lokādetadākarṇya vardhakiḥ kapaṭena gṛhānnirgatya prātaḥsandhyāyāmācchannaḥ samāgatya talpasyādhobhāge sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing this from people, the carpenter deceitfully left the house, then returned secretly at dawn and stayed beneath the bed.

children.text: sā ca jāreṇa saha tatrārūḍhā patyā keśeṣu gṛhītā kathaṃ mucyate
children.translated_text: She climbed onto it with her lover and was seized by the hair by her husband; how could she get free?

children.text: uttaraṃ sā patyā dhṛtā satī dvitīyapatimukhamālokya prāha mayā tava kathitaṃ yadrathakāro mama patirgṛhena vidyate
children.translated_text: The answer: while she was held by her husband, she looked at the face of her second husband and said, "I told you that the chariot-maker, my husband, is in the house.
And he has come; he will at once do what is fitting for you.

children.text: yadyapi pūrvaṃ patyā tvadīyaṃ dravyamapahṛtaṃ tathāpi kṣantavyam
children.translated_text: Although your property was previously stolen by my husband, nevertheless you must forgive him.

children.text: rathakṛti samāgate tava gṛhaṃ gamiṣyāmi yuvayoḥ saṃgatiṃ vā kariṣye
children.translated_text: When the chariot-maker has arrived, I shall go to your house, or I shall bring about a union between you two.
There is no doubt about this."
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
On another day <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot about going.
The parrot said,

children.text: kuru yadrocate kartuṃ yadi vetsi pratīṅgitam
children.translated_text: "Do whatever you wish to do, if you know what has been hinted at,

children.text: śvetāmbareṇa ruddhena yathā pūrvaṃ kṛtaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: as was formerly done by the obstructed <s>Śvetāmbara</s>."
There is a city named <s>Candrapurī</s>.
There a <s>kṣapaṇaka</s> named <s>Siddhasena</s> was honored by the people.

children.text: tasmineva nagare 'nyaḥ sitapaṭo guṇināṃ mukhyaḥ samāgataḥ
children.translated_text: In that same city another white-clad man, foremost among the virtuous, arrived.

children.text: tena ca guṇinā sarvo 'pi jana āvarjitaḥ śrāvakā apyātmāyattāḥ kṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: By that virtuous man all the people were won over, and the lay followers too were made dependent on him.

children.text: sa kṣapaṇako 'pi tasya pūjāṃ kriyamāṇāmasahamānaḥ svayaṃ tadīyopāśraye veśyāṃ preṣayitvā asau veśyālubdho na suśīla iti śvetāmbarasya lokapravādamakarot
children.translated_text: That <s>kṣapaṇaka</s>, unable to tolerate the worship being given to him, himself sent a courtesan to his lodging and spread a public rumor about the <s>Śvetāmbara</s>, saying, "He is attached to courtesans; he is not of good conduct."
He had people summoned to see it.

children.text: brūte ca kṣapaṇakā eva brahmacāriṇaḥ śvetāmbarāstu viplutāḥ
children.translated_text: And he said, "Only the <s>kṣapaṇakas</s> are celibate; the <s>Śvetāmbaras</s> are corrupt."

children.text: so 'pi śvetāmbaro dīpāgninā upādhiṃ prajvālya prabhātaprāptāyāṃ rajanyāṃ nagnobhūya veśyāyā dattahasto nirgataḥ
children.translated_text: But that <s>Śvetāmbara</s>, setting fire to his equipment with the flame of a lamp, when the night had reached dawn, became naked and went out holding the courtesan's hand.
Then public slander arose,
namely, that this man was a <s>kṣapaṇaka</s>, not a white-clad ascetic.
Having heard this, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
On another occasion she set out.
The parrot said:

children.text: yāhi devi na te doṣo yadi jānāsi bhāṣitum
children.translated_text: Go, lady; there is no fault in you, if you know how to speak,
as <s>Ratnādevī</s>, when she was found by her husband together with two lovers.
There is a village called <s>Jalaudā</s>.
There lived a brave prince named <s>Kṣemarāja</s>.
<s>Ratnādevī</s> was his wife.
In that same village there was a village headman named <s>Devasā</s>.
His son was named <s>Dhavala</s>.
Both of them enjoyed <s>Ratnādevī</s>, neither knowing about the other.

children.text: anyadā pitṛputrau tadgṛhasthau yadā tadā rājaputraḥ samāgataḥ
children.translated_text: Once, when father and son were both in her house, the prince arrived.

children.text: tadā kimuttaram śuka āha tatastayā kṛtasaṃjño gṛhādaṅgulyā tarjayannayāt
children.translated_text: What answer did she give then? The parrot said: Then, after she had made a signal to him, he went out of the house, threatening her with his finger.
As he was going away, her husband, frightened, said, 'What is this?'

children.text: tataḥ sā hasantī prāha asya putrastvadgṛhe śaraṇāgataḥ
children.translated_text: Then she said, laughing, 'His son has come to your house for refuge,
and I did not hand him over.
For:

children.text: sa kṣatriyastrāṇasahaḥ satāṃ yastatkārmukaṃ karmasu yasya śaktiḥ
children.translated_text: He is a kṣatriya who is able to give protection; among good men, that is his bow, and his power lies in deeds.
If he bears both kinds of fruitless aims, he makes his speech as though ruined by lack of refinement.
Therefore he is going away angry.
Go; hand over the son.'
And he did just so.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: anyadā prabhāvatī gamanāya śukaṃ pṛcchati sma
children.translated_text: On another occasion <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot about going out.
The parrot said:

children.text: rambhoru gaccha kāmināṃ ko vighnaṃ kartumarhati
children.translated_text: Go, woman with thighs like plantain stems; who can rightly hinder lovers,
if you are able, my lady, to devise a reply, like <s>Mohinī</s>?
There is a city named <s>Śaṅkhapura</s>.
There lived a respectable merchant.
His wife was named <s>Mohinī</s>.

children.text: tāṃ ca bahirgatāṃ kumukho nāma dhūrto ramate
children.translated_text: Whenever she went outside, a rogue named <s>Kumukha</s> enjoyed her.
This was discovered by her husband.
Her husband, however, was extremely timid.

children.text: tato 'sau tāṃ bahiryāntīṃ nivārya pārśvasthita eva tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: So he prevented her from going outside and stayed right beside her.

children.text: tathāpi tayā dhūrtasya kathitaṃ māṃ rātrau bhartṛkhaṭvāsthitāmarvāksuptāṃ bhaja tvam
children.translated_text: Even so, she told the rogue, 'At night, when I am on my husband's bed and lying turned toward him, enjoy me.'
He did so.

children.text: tacca kurvanbhartrāsau puṃścihne dhṛtaḥ kathaṃ gacchatu uttaram dhṛtvā ca patiḥ prāha pradīpamānaya mayā coro dhṛto 'sti
children.translated_text: While he was doing this, the husband seized him by the male organ. How could he get away? Having seized him, the husband said, 'Bring a lamp; I have caught a thief.'
She said, 'I am afraid to go outside.
I will hold him; you bring the lamp.'
And he did so.

children.text: sā ca jāraṃ muktvā gṛhāntarbaddhasya paṭṭakasya jihvāṃ gṛhītvā tathaiva suptā yāvatpatirlakuṭahasto dīpaṃ gṛhītvā samāyātaḥ pṛcchati kimiyaṃ paṭṭakasya jihvā kathamatra tayoktaṃ kṣudhārto 'yam
children.translated_text: She released her lover, grasped the tongue of a calf tied inside the house, and lay down in the same way until her husband came back holding a stick and a lamp. He asked, 'What is this calf's tongue, and how is it here?' She said, 'It is hungry.
It had become thin and weak from drooling after being left untied.
I defeated it in a dispute of statement and reply.

children.text: uktaśca hataka anena pauruṣeṇa kṣayaṃ vrajasi
children.translated_text: And I said to it, "Wretched creature, with this manliness of yours you are going to ruin."'
Thus scolded and ashamed, he went to sleep.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
On another occasion <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot about going out.
The parrot said:

children.text: kṛśodari vrajādya tvaṃ yadi jānāsi bhāṣitum
children.translated_text: Go today, slender-waisted one, if you know how to speak,
as was formerly done by <s>Devikā</s> when she was together with her lover.

children.text: asti kuhāḍākhyo mahāgrāmaḥ tatra jarasākhyo kauṭumbiko mahāmūrkhaḥ
children.translated_text: There is a large village called <s>Kuhāḍa</s>; there lived a very foolish householder named <s>Jarasa</s>.
His wife <s>Devikā</s> was unchaste.

children.text: tāṃ ca prabhākaro brāhmaṇaḥ kṣetramadhye vibhītakavṛkṣasamīpe guptasthāne mudā ramater
children.translated_text: A brahmin named <s>Prabhākara</s> gladly enjoyed her in the middle of a field, near a vibhītaka tree, in a hidden place.

children.text: īdṛśaṃ vyatikaraṃ janācchrutvā tatpatistatrāvalokanāya svayaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard of such an affair from people, her husband himself went there to observe.
Climbing the tree, he saw that very thing.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tatrasthenāpi jalpitam dhūrtike bahudinebhyo 'dya samprāptā ityuktā kathamiyaṃ bhartāraṃ pratyāyayatu
children.translated_text: Although he was there, the lover said, 'Trickster, you have come today after many days.' When she was so addressed, how could she convince her husband?
She said, 'I do not know; you yourself tell me.'
'If you do not go, then I shall tell you.'

children.text: tayā tatheti pratipanne śukaḥ prāha sā ca tadvacaḥ śrutvā taṃ jāraṃ preṣayāmāsa patyā cāvatīrya samāgatena upālabdhā
children.translated_text: When she agreed to that, the parrot said: After hearing his words, she sent that lover away, and when her husband had climbed down and come to her, he reproached her.

children.text: sāha he prabhor īdṛśa eva vṛkṣaḥ atrārūḍhairmithunaṃ dṛśyate
children.translated_text: She said, 'O lord, this tree is just like this: people who climb it see a couple here.'
The husband said, 'You climb up and look.'
She did so.
After she had climbed the tree, she said deceitfully:
'After many days, I have seen you going to another woman.'
That fool thought, 'This is true.'

children.text: sa ca tāṃ śāntayitvā gṛhaṃ nināya
children.translated_text: After pacifying her, he led her home.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: anyedyuḥ prabhāvatī gamanāya śukaṃ pṛcchati sma
children.translated_text: On the next day <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot about going out.
He too said:

children.text: vraja devi vicāraṃ cetkartuṃ jānāsi bhāmini
children.translated_text: Go, lady, if you know how to devise a plan, beautiful woman,

children.text: samaṃ jāreṇa samprāptā sundarīva yathā gṛhe ||
children.translated_text: as <s>Sundarī</s> did when she had come home together with her lover.

children.text: kathametat so 'bravīt asti sīhūlo nāma grāmaḥ
children.translated_text: 'How was that?' He said: There is a village named <s>Sīhūla</s>.
There lived a very wealthy merchant.
His wife was <s>Sundarī</s>.

children.text: tāṃ ca mohano nāma upapatirnityaṃ gṛhamāgatya bhuṅkte
children.translated_text: Her paramour, named <s>Mohana</s>, always came to the house and enjoyed her.

children.text: anyadā yāvatsā tathā tiṣṭhati tāvattatpatiḥ samāgataḥ
children.translated_text: One day, while she was standing there in that way, her husband arrived.
What was she to do?

children.text: uttaram sā patimāgacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā jāraṃ vivastraṃ śikye kṛtvā muktakeśā gṛhānnirgatya dūrasthā patimāha asmadgṛhamadhye nagnabhūtaṃ śikyārūḍhaṃ vidyate
children.translated_text: The answer: Seeing her husband coming, she put her naked lover in a sling, loosened her hair, went out of the house, stood at a distance, and said to her husband, 'Inside our house there is a naked spirit mounted on a sling.'
When she said, 'Go summon exorcists,' that fool went for that purpose.

children.text: tadā ca tadantare tayā ulmukaṃ haste kṛtvā upapatirniṣkāsitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, in the meantime, she took a firebrand in her hand and drove her paramour out.

children.text: patyau ca āgate sā jagāda yadulmukenāpi bhūtaṃ naṣṭam
children.translated_text: And when her husband had returned, she said that even the ghost had been destroyed by the firebrand.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> went to sleep.
